News.title: Police forces spent eye-watering £631m on diversity and equality since murder of George Floyd, says report
News.content:
COP COSTS Police forces spent eye-watering £631m on diversity and equality since murder of George Floyd, says report

Credit: Getty

POLICE forces have spent a whopping £631million on diversity, equality and inclusion programmes since the murder of George Floyd, according to a new report.

The cash could have funded around 2,000 extra frontline officers every year or 8.3 million hours of policing, according to Policy Exchange.



The think tank says the spending came after the introduction of a national Police Race Action Plan after Floyd’s death in Minneapolis in 2020, with nearly three-quarters of UK forces later adopting their own local versions.

It found 87 per cent of forces now have “anti-racist” commitments in their plans, while 58 per cent focus primarily on Black communities.



Policy Exchange says the changes have eroded the principle of policing “without fear or favour” and left officers at risk of treating people differently based on their race.

It comes after two Hampshire officers were placed under investigation over the death of Henry Nowak, who was handcuffed as he lay dying after his killer falsely accused him of carrying out a racist attack.



David Spencer, a former Metropolitan Police detective chief inspector and the report’s author, said: “Police forces have sought to entrench the radical ideology of ‘anti-racism’ into British policing.

“In doing so some police chiefs have set policing against its own foundational principle – to act ‘without fear or favour’.”

Chief Constable Rachel Kearton, chair of the NPCC’s Diversity, Equality and Inclusion Committee, insisted the spending represented “a very small proportion” of the policing budget.

She added: “Improving culture and inclusion is not separate from frontline delivery, it underpins it.



Investment in this area also supports forces in meeting their legal responsibilities.”

News.title: Dramatic moment huge cargo ship sinks in Black Sea as Putin’s armed forces launch strike that ‘killed 10’
News.content:
THIS is the moment a cargo ship sinks in the Black Sea after a deadly Russian missile attack left 10 dead.

Footage shows a suspected dry cargo ship capsizing in Odesa Bay after taking heavy damage from Russian strikes targeting Ukrainian supplies.



The strike comes apart of a wider escalation as Russia retaliates against Ukrainian drone attacks that targeted 200 of its “shadow fleet” of tankers and cargo vessels.

The sunken vessel was reportedly holed several days ago but eventually succumbed to the damage on Sunday.



As the vessel keels over, its massive red-painted hull is exposed before it plunges deeper into the water.

Some Ukrainian outlets identified the stricken vessel as the Turkish-flagged Golden Leo which was likely carrying grain supplies.

The vessel was struck by three Kh-59/Kh-69 cruise missiles while leaving the port in Odesa on July 19, according to reports.

It is understood one of the missiles hit the superstructure on the starboard side after which a fire broke out on the ship.



Ten people were killed as a result.

Eight sailors were evacuated and taken to hospitals.

Another vessel hit in the strike was the AGN Ragnar, a Palau-flagged ship with almost 2,800 tonnes of corn on board.

The Ukrainian pilot and seven crew members were rescued but two Indian sailors are missing after reportedly being thrown into the sea on impact.

Ukrainian officials have previously condemned Russian strikes on grain vessels as potential war crimes.



Russia has stepped up attacks in recent weeks on deepwater ports in southern Ukraine ⁠that ​handle much of the country’s ​grain and other critical cargo.

The retaliations haven’t been limited to the sea – Russia unleashed a 40-minute barrage of ballistic missiles on Kyiv overnight on July 18.

It was one of the most intense blitzes of the war so far.

The action sparked dozens of fires, killed one person and wounded 40.

Among the targets were civilian homes, office buildings, a metro station and a key logistics hub linked to Ukraine‘s armed forces.

News.title: Freeview switch-off could leave Britain dangerously exposed if the internet goes down, ministers warn
News.content:
BRITAIN risks being dangerously exposed if the internet goes down under Government plans to cut off Freeview, ministers have been warned.

The National Preparedness Commission (NPC) said terrestrial television should be protected until at least 2044 over fears using the web alone could cut off the most vulnerable.



A new report concludes that the “tall tower” network carrying digital TV is an asset the UK cannot afford to weaken.

It comes as ministers decide whether to turn off Freeview in 2034 or 2044, and rely on internet streaming services.



The Sun’s Save Our Sets campaign has warned that pensioners and families will be forced to pay for faster broadband on top of the licence fee if terrestrial signals are cut off.

The NPC report found that broadband routers go down immediately after losing power, while TV and DAB radio transmitter sites can stay online for days or even weeks.



It would ensure information could be transmitted to Brits in a national emergency even if the internet had gone down.

The paper adds that the costs of an early switch-off would fall hardest on rural areas with poor broadband connections and few fallback options.

Nigel Huddleston MP, Shadow Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport, said: “It is a fundamental security concern if we lose our emergency broadcasting capability in the event of a cyber attack or internet outage.

“We cannot risk being so vulnerable in these highly uncertain times.”



Lord Toby Harris, who is chairman of the National Preparedness Commission, said: “The UK’s tall tower network is a sovereign, resilient asset that reaches almost every household and supports radio, emergency services and critical infrastructure.

“Protecting terrestrial broadcasting until at least 2044 would preserve a vital, independent route for trusted public information when it is needed most.”

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy last week hinted that ministers would settle on the 2044 date, admitting many believed the earlier switch-off “isn’t possible”.

News.title: Man arrested after ‘stealing 44 bottles of fine wine’ from house evacuated during horror wildfires in France
News.content:
A MAN has been arrested for allegedly breaking into an evacuated house and making off with 44 bottles of fine wine during horror wildfires.

More than 220,000 people have been forced to flee their homes as wildfires ravage southwestern France.



Two huge infernos are ripping towards Bordeaux, with tourists warned to stay away or get out of the region if they’ve already arrived.

Yet as hundreds of thousands flee their homes, authorities are having to step in to stop mass opportunistic break-ins.





One man was arrested in Eysines, Gironde on suspicion of burglary.

Police said the man was stopped in front of an empty home at around 6.15pm on Saturday.

When cops searched his car they found 44 bottles of the finest plonk stowed away inside.

The suspect – already known to police – was arrested and taken into custody.



The arrest comes as French authorities are ready to evacuate the entire city of Bordeaux – “erratic” fire whirlwinds are sending flames ripping towards its nearly one million residents.

Two major wildfires have broken out west of the city and “overwhelmed” firefighters are “far from” bringing the blazes under control.

Local official Sophie Brocas told holidaymakers to stay away and to pack their bags if they have already arrived.



She said: “We urge tourists not to come to this region, at least until the situation is under control.

“I encourage tourists who are already here to consider another destination.”

More than 300,000 people in France and Spain have been forced to flee their homes as fires fuelled by tinder-box conditions and strong winds continue to rage.

Firefighters battling the encroaching blaze in the Gironde area are said to be “overwhelmed” as concerns grow about Bordeaux.

Head Gironde firefighter Sebastien Berge said: “When there’s a fire of this magnitude, it creates its own weather pattern…it’s difficult to monitor.



“Especially when there’s a fire front that stretches for more than 20km (12.5 miles).”

Thousands of evacuees in the area have already been forced to bed down in an exhibition hall as they face an anxious wait over the state of their homes.

Residents and tourists were forced to flee the holiday hotspot Cap Ferret in their droves on Friday as the inferno took hold.

The French military has even been deployed to help battle the blazes.

Meanwhile in Spain, where a national emergency has been declared, favourable weather conditions have helped firefighters in their fight against merging fires outside Madrid.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez conceded there were “complex times ahead”.

A man, believed to be in his 70s, was found dead in his car by firefighters as they extinguished a blaze in Valencia.

News.title: Mystery as decision to charge arthritic 5ft 5in woman, 72, with murder of ‘love rival’ Brit expat stuns French village
News.content:
THE idyllic, honey-bricked Dordogne village of Tremolat has twice been the backdrop for murder.

Eerily, local mother-of-three Marie-Laure Autefort, 70 — a divorced former nurse — has a connection to both.



In 1969, she had a walk-on part in cult horror movie The Butcher, the fictional tale of a woman’s corpse being discovered with multiple blade wounds.

Today, she is centre stage after being charged with the real-life murder of British-South African expat Karen Carter who, in April last year, was discovered bleeding to death after being stabbed eight times.



It has left close-knit Tremolat in deep shock, with many locals perplexed that Marie-Laure is now a prime suspect.

Could a woman of her years, standing less than 5ft 5in tall, who friends say has high blood pressure and severe osteoarthritis in her hands, have the strength and guile to commit such a savage murder?



After all, one of the blade blows almost severed Karen’s arm, while another pierced her kidney and reached her spine.

And was this ferocious assault really a crime of jealousy and passion as investigators now seem to believe?

Many in remote Tremolat — population 600 — had thought Karen’s ­clinical slaying must have been the work of a hired assassin.

In a crime that appears to have been meticulously planned and executed, the murderer arrived and left the scene undetected.



No murder weapon has been found despite fingertip searches, and ­forensic investigators seem to have drawn a blank.

One local said last week: “I’ve always said it was a hit job and I can’t see how they have a case against her [Marie-Laure], but ­perhaps they might have some hard evidence we aren’t aware of.”

Born in South Africa to parents originally from Preston, Lancashire, Karen Carter had intended to see out her years in slow-paced Tremolat.

An attractive brunette of 65 who kept trim playing over-50s football, she and her husband of 30 years, Alan, had first visited the pretty French village from their South African home in 2008.

Karen instantly fell in love with its 12th century charms.



They bought and did up Les Chouettes, a 250-year-old cottage and barn, which Karen managed as holiday lets in summer.

Shortly after his wife’s murder, South African Alan, 66, said: “One of the reasons we bought this property was that Karen had previously been diagnosed with breast cancer and had fought so hard to survive that.

“When we came to the village for the first time, Karen immediately loved it so much that I wanted to make that dream possible.”



Alan, who runs an environmental consultancy and formerly worked at the London Stock Exchange, was keen to keep their base in the South African coastal city of East London, renamed KuGompo City this year.

Yet Karen, who was enamoured with the delights of French rural life, preferred to remain in Tremolat.

The couple — who have four grown- up children, the eldest from Karen’s previous marriage — were soon spending time apart on different continents.

Karen volunteered at Cafe Village, a vibrant community hub and bar, where well-heeled French retirees, British expats and locals mingled over wine and music.

A framed poster of horror flick The Butcher — a claim to fame for Tremolat — hangs on the wall inside the bar.



The movie had portrayed the village as outwardly peaceful and respectable — but with a secret, dark undercurrent.

Another volunteer at the cafe was Paris-born Jean-Francois Guerrier, 75, a retired executive at IT firm Fujitsu.

He and Karen began an affair.

Clutching glasses of wine, the pair were seen dancing and singing to Gloria Gaynor’s I Will Survive in a video posted on the cafe’s Facebook page in December 2024.

However, another woman was also said to hold a candle for urbane Jean-Francois — and that was Marie-Laure Autefort.



Born into a local farming family, she had become infatuated with the retired businessman.

A one-time nurse and carer, she landed her role as an extra in The Butcher aged 12, when filmmakers arrived in the village.

Marie-Laure appeared in a funeral scene where firefighters sprayed the crowd with hoses to make it look like it was raining.



A keen local historian and “intensely proud” of her roots in the village, she has co-authored a book on Tremolat’s history and curated an exhibition of old photos of the place.

It is unclear if she was resentful of wealthy outsiders like Karen who had moved into the village in the years since The Butcher was filmed.

What is certain is her obsessive infatuation with Jean-Francois.

Her brother, retired fireman Philippe Monribot, revealed last year: “She made no secret of the fact she was in love with Guerrier. She was telling everyone in Tremolat, ‘I love him, I love him’.

“He took her to see the chateaux of the Loire Valley, to Paris, to fancy restaurants and so on. She had very little money and fell in love with him — and as soon as he realised that, he bailed on her.”



Others in the village insist it was a one-sided infatuation and accuse Marie-Laure of being a “fantasist”.

Despite Tremolat’s intimate size, Karen is said to have knowingly clapped eyes on Marie-Laure only once, although she was well aware of her existence.

A close friend of the guest house owner said last week that they crossed paths at Cafe Village just six days before the murder.

Jean-Francois was also present.

It was a Wednesday, when the Dordogne Chippy fish-and-chip van visits the bar, and there is music and dancing.



Karen’s friend said: “We hadn’t seen Marie-Laure at Cafe Village for over a year. We were amazed when she turned up with a group of about six friends. She didn’t come over, but Karen picked up on the tense atmosphere. She said, ‘What is it?’.

“I told her Marie-Laure was there and she asked me to point her out. It was common knowledge Marie-Laure was in love with Jean-Francois. She was shouting it from the rooftops.”

Five days later, Karen had dinner with her best friend in the village, Beverly Needham.



Originally from Manchester, Beverly, 69, said last year: “She brought wine, she always did, and I can’t bring myself to move the bottle from where she left it in the kitchen.”

That night, Karen told her friend she had served divorce papers on Alan.

Beverly revealed: “She told me the relationship was over and said, ‘I’m done’ . . . That was her words.”

Alan has subsequently denied Karen filed for divorce and believed the marriage was salvageable.

He had suspected Karen and Jean-Francois were having an affair, but his wife had denied it.



He later revealed: “I told her the gossip was tarnishing her reputation, but she said there was nothing in it. She told our friends the same.”

On April 29, 2025 — the evening after Beverly and Karen’s dinner — Jean-Francois held a wine tasting at his hilltop property on the outskirts of Tremolat.

The 15 guests, including Karen, left around 10pm. Karen — who had turned 65 two days before — drove her Dacia Duster the five minutes to her Les Chouettes guest house. It was a mild, overcast evening.

A light wind rippled through the walnut trees around the property.

Karen exited the vehicle, opened the front door and turned on the light.



Returning to the Dacia, she leaned into the back seat to pick up her crossbreed puppy, Haku.

The killer then emerged from the shadows and launched into a “frenzied” assault with what the police believe was a long-bladed knife.

Karen’s body was found soon after by distraught Jean-Francois, who had come to spend the night with her.



He later told a friend it was a scene of “just gore”.

A day later, cops arrested Marie- Laure and questioned her for around 40 hours.

She was released without charge after giving a credible alibi.

For the next 14 months, the investigation seemed to be going nowhere.

Marie-Laure’s brother Philippe said cops had turned up at his house on the edge of the village with a search warrant on five separate occasions as they hunted for the murder weapon.



Tremolat-born, police hoped he could guide them in a search of nearby caves. Nothing was found.

Now, it has emerged Marie-Laure was charged with Karen’s murder on July 2 after “inconsistencies” were found in her alibi.

An investigating source said: “She made out she was looking after somebody that night, but the facts were very vague.”

Marie-Laure denies any wrongdoing. She was released on bail on the condition she doesn’t stay in Tremolat.

A friend says the osteoarthritis in her hands has left her “barely able to cut open an envelope”, let alone wield a blade.



Philippe said it was “impossible” to imagine his sister could be involved in murder, adding she was “scared of going out in the dark”.

Prosecutors have not ruled out further arrests.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

An investigating source told The Sun there was “the possibility the suspect may have been working with someone else — somebody who was a lot stronger and fitter”.

Meanwhile, idyllic Tremolat will be under a dark pall until whoever killed Karen Carter is behind bars.

News.title: Man dies & one taken to hospital after ‘getting into difficulty’ in sea at popular UK beach
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SEASIDE TRAGEDY Man dies & one taken to hospital after ‘getting into difficulty’ in sea at popular UK beach

A MAN has died after getting into difficulty while in the sea at a popular UK beach.

Emergency services rushed to the coast near Pound Road near West Wittering beach at around 2.30pm on Sunday.



The force pulled two men out from the sea and sadly pronounced one dead at the scene, while the other was taken to hospital.

A West Wittering Beach spokesperson said: “Our thoughts and sincere condolences are with the man’s family, friends and all those affected by this tragic incident.



“We would like to thank our lifeguards, emergency service colleagues and members of the public who assisted during the response.”

Sussex Police were called to the area following reports of two men getting into difficulty in the sea near the Beach Café.

A police spokesperson said: “Both were pulled from the sea and received treatment from emergency services at the scene.

“Sadly, one of the men was pronounced dead at the scene.

“The other man has been taken to hospital as a precaution.

“Next of kin have been informed and the matter has been passed to the coroner’s officer.”



Pictures taken from the beach show coastguard and ambulance vehicles parked up next to the water.

It is believed the men did not know each other.

They were given medical treatment at the scene.

The family of the deceased person has been informed.

News.title: I’ll quit if Burnham fails to find billions to rebuild Britain’s Armed Forces, vows new Defence Sec Wes Streeting
News.content:
DEFENCE Secretary Wes Streeting yesterday vowed to quit if PM Andy Burnham fails to stump up the billions needed to rebuild Britain’s Armed Forces.

The Cabinet minister said fully funding Labour’s Defence Investment Plan was a “matter of principle” and said he would resign if the money failed to materialise.



The Government must plug a £4.7billion black hole in the plan over the next five years, on top of finding £10.3billion of savings from elsewhere across Whitehall.

Mr Streeting insisted that the DIP “will be fully funded” with Chancellor John Healey expected to set out the specifics at future fiscal events.



It comes as Mr Burnham refused to commit to lifting defence spending to three per cent of GDP.

He told the BBC his “first challenge” was making sure the DIP was fully-funded ahead of the Budget, but would not give an answer to when exactly Britain would reach the three per cent target.

Mr Healey long championed the demand himself before he entered the Treasury.

He quit as Sir Keir Starmer’s Defence Secretary over the failure to stick to a firm timetable for the key spending target.

The Office for Budget Responsibility has estimated reaching three per cent by the end of the decade would cost an extra £17.3billion a year.

Meanwhile, Mr Streeting backed Donald Trump’s calls for Europe to shoulder more of the burden for its own security — but insisted the Government would not “suck up” to the US President.



Mr Burnham also said he would put the UK’s interests first in dealings with Mr Trump, even if it means disagreeing with him.

News.title: Burnham must not make the same mistakes Starmer made with Trump – and show his govt can deliver on defence and migration
News.content:
Frenemy States

ARE Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Defence Secretary Wes Streeting trying to repair the Special Relationship, damaged by Sir Keir Starmer’s Government?

Both had previously insulted Donald Trump, but in a charm offensive directed at our American allies, the PM described the “warm” 20-minute phone chat he had with the President last week while Streeting admits Britain would ultimately thank Trump for pushing it to spend properly on defence.



And yet, to appease Trump-hating Labour MPs, Streeting explicitly insisted the UK should not “suck up” to the President while Burnham — channeling Hugh Grant’s Love Actually PM — said he would be prepared to call out Trump to defend UK national interests.

They should not make the same mistakes Starmer made.



Sir Keir saw himself as something of a “Trump-whisperer” . . . until the President saw through his ineptitude.

And he talked a great game on defence spending but couldn’t back it with cash.

At least Streeting has vowed to resign if Labour’s Defence Investment Plan is not funded, but that’s a long way from lifting defence spending to 3 per cent of GDP by 2030.

We’ll see how Trump’s warmth evaporates if Burnham’s Government fails to meet Nato obligations, exploit our oil and gas reserves under the North Sea; or halt the flow of illegal migrants to our shores.

Actions speak louder than words.

Sick greed

“WE’RE going really hard at the layers of bureaucracy in the NHS,” said Wes Streeting when he was Health Secretary last year and record numbers of NHS bosses were revealed to be earning more than £110,000.



But the Health Service’s army of pen-pushers is not going down without a fight.

New figures show the number of NHS managers earning £300,000+ has more than doubled in a year.

With pay supposedly linked to performance, you would think the NHS must now be twice as efficient. And faultless. Fat chance.

New Health Secretary Yvette Cooper needs to finish what Streeting at least tried to start.

Wet blankets

BLEEDING-heart social workers and judges keep falling over themselves to protect guilty foreign crooks at the expense of law-abiding Brits.



But halting the deportation of an Albanian cocaine-dealer because it might worsen his daughter’s bed-wetting is a new low.

Expect every vile criminal to now use similar excuses to get what they want.

Human rights law has gone beyond a joke.

News.title: Toddler escapes death after suffering cocaine overdose as man arrested
News.content:
Toddler escapes death after suffering cocaine overdose as man arrested

A 39-year old man was arrested after calling for help after the two-year-old began struggling to breathe, with paramedics administering a NARCAN nasal spray which the boy responded to

View 2 Images Alexander T. Moles was arrested on charges of child endangerment (Image: Cape May County Prosecutor Office)

A toddler has nearly died after overdosing on cocaine, with first responders forced into action after the two-year-old was found struggling to breathe. Police on the Jersey Shore in the United States confirmed they have arrested a man, 39-year-old Alexander T. Moles, on charges of child endangerment after a July 20 callout in relation to a sick toddler. When first responders arrived, it was discovered that had been on his way to hospital, driving the two-year-old to A&E as he was having difficulty breathing. Paramedics administered two doses of Naloxone nasal spray - also known as NARCAN - to the boy, to which he responded. NARCAN is an anti-opioid drug which has no effect on a patient if there are no opioids in their system.

View 2 Images FILE IMAGE: A white powdery substance in a small, clear plastic bag similar to what police found at Moles' Airbnb (Image: eliosdnepr – stock.adobe.com)

The two-year-old boy was then transportedto Cooper University Hospital Cape Regional for further medical attention, with blood tests later confirming the tot had tested positive for cocaine.

Police officers later found a pill, tinfoil packets labelled “tapentadol hydrochloride,” a clear plastic bag containing a white, powdery substance, and several short plastic straws following a judge-ordered search of Moles’s Airbnb, according to an affidavit.

As per a statement released by prosecutors in New Jersey, a joint investigation was then initiated by the Wildwood Police Department and the Cape May County Prosecutor’s Office Special Victims Unit. A spokesperson said: "Through the investigation it was determined that Alexander T. Moles was vacationing at a residence in Wildwood, New Jersey when the two-year-old male became ill.

Article continues below

"As a result of the initial investigation, on July 21, 2026, Alexander T. Moles was arrested and charged with one count of Endangering the Welfare of a Child, a crime of the second degree; one count of Possession of Cocaine, a crime of the third degree; one count of Possession of Drug Paraphernalia, a Disorderly Persons Offence; and one count of Possession of Prescription Legend Drugs, a crime of the fourth degree.

The Cape May County Prosecutor's Office added: "Prosecutor Sutherland advises persons convicted of a second degree crime are subject to a term of imprisonment of five to 10 years in New Jersey State Prison. A person convicted of a third degree crime are subject to a term of imprisonment of three to 5 years in New Jersey State Prison." The 39-year-old was arrested and placed in the Cape May County Correctional Facility, but was released three days later on bail with conditions.

News.title: Tragic final moments of innocent boy, 12, gunned down riding his new bike to the shops
News.content:
Tragic final moments of innocent boy, 12, gunned down riding his new bike to the shops

Jacob Freytes only received the hand-me-down bike a day earlier, neighbours said, as New York mayor Zohran Mamdani has condemned the killing, thought to be the result of gangland violence

View 3 Images Jacob was 12, had a new bike, and just wanted to go to the shops (Image: Facebook/El Nene Kai)

A 12-year-old has been tragically shot dead outside a New York City corner shop while nipping out on his new bike.

‌



Jacob Freytes was gunned down shortly before 5pm on Saturday (July 25) in The Bronx. CCTV showed Jacob was hit by a stray bullet outside the Wanda Deli Grocery on Elliott Place.

‌



He then ‘staggered’ back inside the shop, clutching his chest, before tragically passing away, reports the New York Post.

‌



“I saw him just before he left,” neighbour Walter Calon, 56, recalled. “I shook his hand and said, ‘look out for your little brother and sister.’

View 3 Images The Wanda Deli Grocery on Elliott Place, in The Bronx, where Jacob Freytes died (Image: Google Maps)

“And then less than a half-hour later, I got a call from my mom and I just dropped the phone right out of my hand.”

‌



Jacob’s father is retired NYPD sergeant Jesus Freytes, the news outlet said. It appears Jacob’s killing was a case of being in ‘the wrong place at the wrong time’, his distraught friend, Marlyn Rosario, said.

It’s thought Jacob cycled to the convenience store — known as bodegas in New York — on a hand-me-down bike he only received a day earlier.

Marlyn’s mother, Miledy Rosario, said she bought her daughter a new bike and gave it to Jacob on Friday (July 24) after his parents agreed to the gift.

‌



Jacob’s area of The Bronx, Mount Eden, is reportedly known for its gang violence. Police are now investigating if the two most notorious organised crime groups — Trinitarios and Sev Side Pinni — are behind the killing.

Allegedly, the killer got into an altercation outside Wanda Deli Grocery which escalated up to the point where a gun was pulled and fired.

View 3 Images Mayor Zohran Mamdani has condemned the killing (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



Another two people were hurt in the incident, according to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. He condemned the violence in a statement released hours after Jacob’s death.

Mayor Mamdani said: “A 12-year-old was shot and killed in the Bronx earlier today. My heart breaks for his family, friends and all those who loved him.

“Their loss is unimaginable. I am praying for the speedy recovery of the other two victims of this shooting. I’m grateful for the hospital staff, and the NYPD for their work to find those responsible for this heinous act.

‌



“Our children should be able to ride their bikes on a nice summer day in their neighbourhood without fear of being shot. We cannot accept this violence as normal.”

Both of Jacob’s parents are said to be ‘devastated’. Mount Eden neighbours have remembered the 12-year-old as ‘a bright kid’.

Walter Calon added: “He always saluted me.

‌



“He was a bright kid. He played sports — he’s always playing here in the front court.

“I saw him grow up. He’s a good kid. I don’t understand.’’

Julio Lopez, close to the Freytes family, said: “He was adventurous. He was a free spirit. He was different. He lived on his own terms, and he was only 12.

Article continues below

“He was happy. He was chipper. He was saying hi to the guys up the block. He showed respect. He was a good kid.”

News.title: Boy, 16, charged with murder after teenager 'stabbed to death' at skate park
News.content:
Boy, 16, charged with murder after teenager 'stabbed to death' at skate park

Bedfordshire Police said a 17-year-old boy was rushed to hospital following the incident in Kingsway Recreation Ground, Luton, shortly after 6.30pm on Friday

View 2 Images Bedfordshire Police at the scene in Luton (Image: Bedfordshire Police)

Police have charged a 16-year-old boy with murder after a 17-year-old was fatally stabbed at a UK skate park.

Three teenagers have also been arrested as part of an ongoing investigation into the fatal stabbing of a 17-year-old boy in Luton on Friday (July 24).

The victim was taken to hospital with multiple stab wounds but sadly died shortly afterwards, police said.

The further three 17-year-old boys were arrested on Saturday (July 25) and Sunday (July 26) all on suspicion of murder, violent disorder and carrying a weapon.

A 16-year-old boy who was arrested on Friday has since been charged with murder and remanded in custody.

Another 17-year-old boy, also arrested on Friday who was being treated in hospital for serious injuries, is now in police custody.

Detective Chief Inspector Nick Gardener said: “We are progressing our investigation, and we are continuing to appeal to anyone who was in the area, or witnessed the events leading up to the disorder to please get in touch.

View 2 Images Police received reports of a number of teenagers carrying large knives at Kingsway Recreation Ground (Image: Google Maps)

“Our officers are continuing to carry our additional high-visibility patrols, and we are continuing to engage with local members of the public.

“We would also like to remind the public not to share any distressing videos or images as this can be concerning for families involved, but also form a vital part of the police investigation.”

Gardener has expressed wishes of condolences to the victim family on Friday. He said on the day: "Horrific violence in Luton has sadly cost a teenage boy his life today.

"Our thoughts are first and foremost with the loved ones of the boy who lost his life in such tragic circumstances."

Article continues below

Anyone with information is urged to visit the Bedfordshire Police website or call 101 and quote reference Operation Crownbeacon.

News.title: Police appeal to find missing teen girl last seen five days ago in Gloucester
News.content:
Police appeal to find missing teen girl last seen five days ago in Gloucester

Leinah, 17, was last seen at around 7.30am on Tuesday with cops exhausting several lines of enquiry before now turning to the public for help finding her

View 2 Images Seventeen-year-old Leinah has been missing for five days (Image: Gloucestershire Police)

People are being asked to dial 999 if they see a teen girl who has been missing for five days.

‌



17-year-old Leinah went missing from Gloucester on Tuesday 21 July, police have said.

‌



She was last seen at around 7.30am and left an address in the Hempstead area on foot shortly afterwards before vanishing with concerns growing for her welfare.

‌



Gloucestershire Police said it has already completed a number of enquiries in the search for the missing teen before now asking for the public's help.

Today the force has appealed for information and released two images citing concerns for Leinah.

‌



View 2 Images She was last seen wearing blue jeans, a black hoodie, white trainers and carrying a small, cream handbag (Image: Gloucestershire Police)

She is described as being around 5ft 2ins tall, of a slim build and with long brown hair which she may be wearing in a ponytail or claw clip.

She was last seen wearing blue jeans, a black hoodie, white trainers and carrying a small, cream handbag.

Article continues below

Anyone who has seen Leinah or knows of her whereabouts is being asked to contact police on 101 quoting reference 53260062654.

Alternatively, if you u can see her at the time of calling, Gloucestershire Police have said to dial 999 instead and ask for police.

News.title: Andy Burnham to meet Volodymyr Zelensky as Ukraine President becomes first world leader to visit PM in UK
News.content:
Andy Burnham to meet Volodymyr Zelensky as Ukraine President becomes first world leader to visit PM in UK

Volodymyr Zelensky and Andy Burnham are going to meet on a British naval base on Monday - as Britain shares vital know-how on how to make state-of-the-art Stone Cloak jammers to prevent Russia tracking drones

View 3 Images Volodymyr Zelensky will become the first world leader to meet Andy Burnham in the UK (Image: PA)

Volodymyr Zelensky will become the first world leader to meet Andy Burnham, as the two hold a crunch meeting in the UK on Monday.

‌



The Ukrainian President is expected to join the Prime Minister at a British naval base, where the PM will share vital know-how to help produce state-of-the-art electronic jammers to block Russian defence systems. This will allow Ukraine to mass produce devices, known as Stone Cloak, to prevent its drones being tracked and targeted.

‌



Mr Burnham described the technology as "the best of homegrown British innovation". He said: "Britain stands with Ukraine, shoulder to shoulder, and our support remains unwavering. Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve, and we will not back down until we achieve long-lasting and just peace for Ukraine.

‌



"Stone Cloak is the best of homegrown British innovation and proven on the frontline, and it will be vital to protecting our security in both our countries."

View 3 Images Andy Burnham said the UK's support for Ukraine remains steadfast (Image: GETTY)

No10 said the UK is sharing the intellectual property for Stone Cloak, which will be built into the next generation of UK deep-strike capabilities. The British military will use the jammers to enhance Project Brakestop - the UK's new low-cost cruise missile. Thousands of the tablet-sized devices have already been gifted to Ukraine to help with drone operations.

‌



No10 said the move knocks Russia a step back in Putin's illegal invasion on Ukraine. During Mr Zelensky's visit, he and Mr Burnham will meet more than 200 Ukrainian military personnel and sailors who have been training in the UK for the past three weeks.

The UK has previously pledged £3billion a year to Ukraine to help fight Russia for as long as it takes - providing a total of £25bn in support since 2022.

It comes as Mr Burnham revealed he was prepared to stand up to Donald Trump, if it were in Britain's national interest. In an interview with the BBC, to be screened in full on Monday, he said: "Well, I've had one phone call. I always treat people as I find them, and it was a good exchange. It was, as I said before, a warm exchange.

‌



View 3 Images Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he has held talks with his US counterpart (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

"So I am that kind of politician, I always judge people as I find them. I've lived my whole life by that. And I found him to be really warm on Monday. But obviously we will continue to build the relationship as we go forward."

Pressed by journalist Laura Kuenssberg on whether he would be prepared to call out the President if needed, Mr Burnham said: "Of course... all leaders have to do that. You have to defend your own national interest before anything else.

‌



"That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly. I will always put Britain's interests first." His predecessor, Keir Starmer, had a difficult relationship with the US President after he refused to allow US forces to use British bases to launch aggressive strikes on Iran.

On Sunday new Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he had spoken to US counterpart Pete Hegseth, and made clear that position would continue. But he stated the two nations were working together on reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

The vital shipping route, which transports 20% of the world's natural gas and oil supplies, has been effectively shut by Iran after the US and Israel launched attacks on February 28.

‌



Mr Streeting told Sky News: "I was clear that we've not supported offensive action in Iran and we won't support offensive action in Iran, but there are plenty of things that we can and should do together when it comes to securing the Strait of Hormuz, in making sure that Iran doesn't develop nuclear weapons, in terms of investing in our capability and Nato's capability."

He said the closure is having a big economic impact and admitted: "But it's hard to undertake that work, of clearing the strait and securing commercial shipping while hostilities continue. And that's why every effort is being made, particularly by allies in the region, to try and bring about the conditions where we can achieve that."

Describing relations with the Trump administration he said: "The first thing you do is you don't suck up. And I don't think, my impression is, President Trump, his administration, that's not what they're looking for, actually. He's a straight talker."

Article continues below

Asked if he trusts the US President, the Defence Secretary said: "Well, I don't know him, but I do trust the United States." He said the relationship between the two nations is unlike any in the world.

At the weekend John Healey, the new Chancellor, promised a "buy British" blitz within the UK government. He told The Sun: "You will see this as a determined drive that you have not seen before from a British government. Buying British not 'if possible', but by design. So every procurement pound supports British jobs, British apprenticeships and British skills."

He pointed out that when he was Defence Secretary, over 86% of the 1,200 major defence contracts handed out went to British firms. The government is yet to set a timetable for reaching 3% of the UK's gross domestic product (GDP) on defending the nation. Mr Healey told the Sun this was "not a matter for this first week".

News.title: Cruel owner made three dogs live in house of horror in smashed glass and broken furniture
News.content:
Cruel owner made three dogs live in house of horror in smashed glass and broken furniture

Connor Stewart pleaded guilty to breaching animal welfare legislation after his three dogs were found living in "appalling" conditions and were underweight with visible ribs showing

View 3 Images The three dogs were found underweight and living in horrific conditions (Image: SSPCA)

A cruel pet owner made his three dogs live among smashed glass and broken furniture until they were rescued.

‌



The poor pups had no access to food and water, and their living conditions were described as "appalling" by animal welfare groups. Their owner, Connor Stewart, pleaded guilty to breaching animal welfare legislation.

‌



It was clear the dogs' living conditions were horrendous, even when Scottish SPCA inspectors looked through the letterbox of the Livingstone home. Stewart was told to return to the flat and give them access and, after arriving, brought Dobermans Ammo and Karma and Staffordshire Bull Terrier Kya out onto the landing area.

‌



View 3 Images The dogs lived in filthy conditions (Image: Scottish SPCA/PA Wire)

Anyone who spots stray cats on holiday urged to do one thing READ MORE :

Ammo was underweight, with his ribs and hips obviously visible and his nails overgrown. An inspector said: "The flat was completely squalid. The floors were soaked in urine and covered in thick layers of faeces throughout the property, some of which was beginning to turn mouldy. There was broken furniture throughout, smashed glass on the floors and electric shock collars charging in the kitchen area of the flat.

‌



"All the food and water bowls were empty and bone dry." These conditions were some of the worst the inspector had found animals living in and the decision was made to remove all dogs from the property and take them into the care of the Scottish SPCA.

View 3 Images The floors were soaked in urine and covered in layers of faeces (Image: Scottish SPCA/PA Wire)

Police Scotland were called to support removal of the animals, but Stewart fled with his two Dobermans. His remaining Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Kya was taken to a local veterinary practice for further care.

Article continues below

The poor pooch smelled strongly of urine and faeces and drank voraciously having had no water. After pleading guilty, Stewart was sentenced last week and has been banned from owning, keeping or caring for animals for five years. He was also fined £200.

The inspector added: "We are pleased with the Sheriff's decision. Stewart's behaviour was unacceptable, and he showed complete disregard for his dogs' wellbeing.

"No animal should be kept in such conditions, and we hope this sentencing sends a clear message that animal neglect will not be tolerated in Scotland."

News.title: 'Future of Andy Burnham's mission to transform Britain rests on dodging Starmer's destructive defence targets'
News.content:
Ruinous rises for a spendthrift Ministry of Defence are a bullet Andy Burnham and John Healey either dodge or Labour’s fresh commanders will shoot a revitalised UK government in the foot.

Because the blunt choice is between prioritising higher living standards, social care and council houses or throwing away good money after bad without any proof Britain would be better protected militarily. The new Prime Minister signalled he’s spotted the trap in refusing to commit to predecessor Keir Starmer’s £80billion annual target of 3% GDP by 2030, up £10bn a year, in his BBC interview.

For Healey, now charged with finding money after quitting as Starmer’s Defence Secretary with an incendiary claim the country wasn’t safe, the dilemma is deeply personal as well as highly political. Stick to Starmer’s destructive Nato 3.5% guns and that would soar to £140bn by 2035, requiring a £40bn increase in today’s prices. The respected Institute for Government think-tank warned that is the equivalent to two-thirds of the schools budget or the combined budgets of the Home Office and Ministry of Justice.

View 4 Images Andy Burnham (Image: Paul Marriott/Shutterstock)

‌



Streeting says he wouldn't have accepted Defence Secretary job without Burnham spending promise READ MORE :

Welfare vs warfare may over-simplify options but unless the PM and Chancellor find a giant pot of gold there would be trade-offs. And unless a political-industrial-military consensus (all major national parties save the Greens are locked in a ludicrous game of Play Your Cards Right shouting “higher”) is challenged an MoD damned for “unbelievable” waste by decorated Colonel Al Carns who resigned alongside Healey will be a disastrous drain.

We need Burnham to state Britain is already the world’s sixth biggest defence spender and towards the head of the Nato pack in share of national wealth. The basic idea of Nato is Britain never stands alone which is a double relief given the MoD’s record of paying more for late and worse armoured vehicles and warships.

My hunch is the PM will duck and dive rather than disown Starmer’s legacy of unrealistic, unnecessary international targets as he tries to fill a £5bn black hole. For Healey, it’s much tricker, though he could drop into conversations the 500,000 men GCHQ spy centre’s chiefs believes Russia has lost in Ukraine means Putin’s bled his country dry.

One of Burnham’s new ministers told me the percentage targets were madness. The PM might agree.

‌



The future of his mission to transform Britain for everybody rests on missing them.

Farage's pop-up prison hypocrisy

Had to laugh when flailing Farage proposed pop-up “Nightingale” prisons on MoD land to ease overcrowding when kneejerk Nigel and Reform routinely back locals campaigning against holding asylum seekers in redundant army camps.

I don’t imagine villagers and townies would welcome thousands of criminals plopped on their doorsteps in makeshift, insecure huts and I bet hypocritical Farage would join the outrage.

View 4 Images Farage's 'Nightingale' hypocrisy (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

‌



Burnham, who is reviewing who might be let out early to free cells for fresh convicts, inherited a poisonous Sophie’s Choice from the Con-servatives which bedevilled Starmer but this is an issue exposing Reform’s vacuous gimmickry.

Running away from debating a bin in his Clacton farce, Farage wants to talk about everything except his £5million secret bung, aristo “Posh George” Cottrell paying his bills and now London private bank Arbuthnot Latham freezing Reform’s account for two weeks during the general election over potentially illegal donations.

Fleet is the real deal

Burnham enjoyed a sure-footed first week but one misstep was not finding a new job for Natalie Fleet, the Bolsover MP whose own rape traumas prevented her from continuing as Safeguarding Minister.

Groomed, raped and made pregnant aged 15 by an older man and revealing she was raped in her sleep by another, the strength she finds to speak publicly is heroic.

‌



View 4 Images Natalie Fleet is the real deal

That Fleet doesn’t consider herself brave or courageous is another reason this working class marvel who speaks for and inspires millions of other women feeling ignored should’ve been shuffled into another post. Be it making welfare work, sorting social care or building houses, the point is we need people not robots in power – and fighter Fleet is the real deal.

Inciting the dross

No great surprise most thugs arrested during last month’s mindless violence after the jailing of student Henry Nowak’s cynical murderer had previously been reported to police for domestic abuse.

I say no great surprise because two in five arrested after summer 2024 disturbances in parts of the country following the Southport murders had similarly been reported for domestic abuse.

‌



Hard Right and Far Right politicians incite the dross to riot. Entirely separately, have you heard their deafening silence since the arrest of influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate on 59 charges of rape, violent assault, trafficking girls and the indecent images of a child? Bet it would be a different story if they were Muslims.

Going Up

Brickie turned Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram is the most important building block in Andy Burnham’s team.

As long as these Scousers stay friends the new PM’s feet are on the ground. Fall out and it’ll be like the ravens leaving the Tower of London.

Going Down

Blocked standing again for the Cons by Kemi Badenoch because she doesn’t think him extreme enough, ex-party chair Grant Shapps should reapply under his get-rich-quick pseudonym Michael Green. The Tories always love a scammer.

News.title: Berlin Pride crash updates: Suspect shot dead by police after terror attack
News.content:
Berlin attack shows why Pride is still necessary, Streeting says

Wes Streeting says last night's attack shows why Pride marches are necessary.

The defence secretary said incidents like yesterday's are "becoming far too common on our television screens".

"I would say to people, especially at a time when Pride marches have come in for some challenge: why do we have Pride marches? Why are they necessary in this country? Hasn't this all changed?," Streeting told Sky News.

"In many respects, things are different and better now than they've ever been [...] But hate crimes are also on the rise. There are lots of people who don't accept diversity and difference in our society.

Wes Streeting (file image) (Image: SKY NEWS)

"And that's why pride is a celebration. But it's also a protest against those who do not accept life in the 21st century, do not accept people loving each other in same-sex relationships and in the very worst cases would seek to do us harm."

Asked about possible threats to the upcoming Brighton Pride parade, he added that the event would be "well policed" and "get the balance right in terms of policing".

"The home secretary will [...] make the right determinations around what kind of policing presence we need," he said.

News.title: Badenoch says PM must rule out tax rises to fund social care reform
News.content:
Kemi Badenoch has written to the prime minister asking him to "rule out any tax rises or increased borrowing" to fund social care reform.

In a letter to Andy Burnham, the Conservative Party leader said she would be happy to work with him to find a solution, but only if he sticks to her party's "two core principles".

She said any reform must be funded by reducing current spending and not raising taxes, and also be fair to those who have "made provisions and saved up over the course of their lives".

Burnham is expected to make a speech on adult social care this week. A No 10 source said this was part of his plan to "run towards problems that have been neglected".

News.title: Girlguiding unveils first major uniform redesign since 1990
News.content:
The organisation said the uniform combines the charity's heritage with modern colours and prints.

The range is made up of 30 items of clothing, 15 accessories and neckerchiefs - with prices starting at Â£12, for a T-shirt.

Design features include hidden pockets in waist bands, thumb holes, and badge sashes which double as cross-body bags.

This is the first time in 30 years Girlguiding has updated its entire range at the same time.

Oswald said the range was "all about providing girls with the freedom to express themselves, whilst feeling part of our amazing organisation".

Members do not have to buy the new range straightaway, the website explains, and they can continue to wear the old uniform until they need a replacement.

A Girlguiding survey in June of 2,000 girls aged six to 16 in the UK found that 93% said they felt most comfortable when able to choose how they styled themselves.

Angellica Bell, a Girlguiding ambassador and presenter, said the new design gives "girls and volunteers the freedom to style it the way that suits them".

She added: "The new uniform empowers girls and volunteers to embrace their individuality."

News.title: Littler wins Matchplay and smashes Taylor record
News.content:
Luke Littler defended his World Matchplay title in sensational style - and smashed Phil Taylor's tournament and final average records in the process.

The 19-year-old beat seventh seed Gerwyn Price 18-9 in Blackpool to become just the fourth person to win back-to-back Matchplay titles.

World number one Littler finished the week with an average of 111.04, beating Taylor's record of 106.31 in 2010.

He averaged 111.53 in the final, setting a new record as he bettered Taylor's 111.23 against Adrian Lewis in 2013.

Littler claimed Â£225,000 in prize money for winning the event and now has Â£3,143,500 over the PDC's two-year order of merit. That is Â£2.13m more than Luke Humphries in second spot.

"It's been a crazy week, one of the best weeks of my life with the darts I've played," Littler told Sky Sports.

"It's been tough. The stats may look like it's easy, but when you're on this stage with how hot it is, it's not easy."

Price averaged 104.97 in the final and has enjoyed a successful week, climbing to fourth in the order of merit and reclaiming the Welsh number one spot from Jonny Clayton.

News.title: UK's most parched regions miss chance for rain ahead of next heatwave
News.content:
Some of the driest regions of the UK have missed their chances for rain ahead of another heatwave beginning this week.

Parts of the northern and western UK saw some rainfall over the weekend, with further showers and unsettled conditions expected over the next few days.

But southern parts of the country - where the least amount of rain has fallen - are set to see temperatures climb once again, with more dry and sunny weather in the forecast.

It comes as parts of Wales have officially entered drought status, while parts of southern, central and eastern England remain in "prolonged dry weather", the final stage before drought is declared.

The coming days will only exacerbate dry conditions as another heatwave is expected to be declared, with temperatures peaking around 35C (95F) in south-east England.

In advance of the high temperatures, heat health alerts have been issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

The south-west, south-east, London, East of England, West and East Midlands and Yorkshire and The Humber are all under the alerts from 9:00 BST on Tuesday 28 July until 9:00 BST on Friday 31 July.

The UKHSA warns that heat is expected to cause minor impacts for health and social care services, with an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

News.title: Four people including baby die after car crash
News.content:
Four people, including a baby, have died after a car crashed into trees on a busy dual carriageway in Derby.

Emergency services were called after a red Hyundai car left the A38 and crashed into trees - between the A50 Toyota Island and the A516 - at about 23:00 BST on Saturday.

Derbyshire Police said the passengers, two women, 18 and 30, and a man, 36, died at the scene. The baby girl was taken to hospital where she died shortly after.

The force said the driver, a 33-year-old man, was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving. He was subsequently taken to hospital for serious injuries.

Police said all those involved were from Leeds in West Yorkshire, adding their relatives have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

"Our thoughts are with them at this most distressing time," a spokesperson said.

The carriageway was closed for several hours while emergency services dealt with the crash, but it has since been reopened.

Anyone who witnessed the crash or has any dashcam footage has been urged to contact police.

News.title: Trump paused attacks on Iran to make space for talks, US ambassador says
News.content:
President Donald Trump has paused attacks on Iran for the second night in a row to give diplomacy more time, the US ambassador to the UN said.

Speaking to Fox News on Sunday, ambassador Mike Waltz said the president was "giving talks some space, he's giving it a little bit of room".

An Iranian army spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had halted "retaliatory" attacks in the region in response.

The pause follows nearly two weeks of daily US strikes and tit-for-tat attacks, effectively unravelling the ceasefire struck in June.

Asked whether Trump had decided against escalation for now, Waltz told NBC: "I wouldn't go that far at all. The president is keeping all options on the table."

Waltz also rejected reports in the New York Times, external that administration officials had warned expanding hostilities could dangerously drain a diminished stockpile of air defence munitions.

"The US military... has everything that it needs to conduct this campaign as effectively as it needs to be," he said.

As of Sunday evening, Trump had not spoken publicly on the latest developments, but earlier posted computer-generated images on his Truth Social account that depicted US military planes bombing Iranian ships and Kharg island.

Meanwhile, Iran and Oman held several rounds of technical talks in Tehran on Friday and Saturday to discuss management of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei.

Disputes over control of the strait reignited US-Iran tensions earlier this month and it remains a major block to permanently ending the war.

Iran and the US signed a memorandum of understanding in June to halt military operations and reopen the strait, as well as to reach an agreement to end the war over the following 60 days.

But after Iranian forces attacked tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on 13 July, the US resumed airstrikes on the country and reinstated its naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran retaliated with attacks on US military facilities and bases across the Middle East, killing four American soldiers. The US strikes have since killed dozens of people, according to Iran's health ministry.

In the UK, new Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he would meet his US counterpart Pete Hegseth in the coming week to discuss the strait, which is one of the world's key transport routes for oil, liquid natural gas and other essential commodities.

"When it comes to securing maritime freedom and free commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, that's where we are absolutely aligned," Streeting told the BBC.

Earlier this week, oil prices hit $100 a barrel for the first time since May, as the renewed fighting stoked fears over global energy supplies.

As the war nears its fifth month, it remains largely unpopular in the US, with a new poll from CBS/YouGov suggesting 57% of Americans are frustrated about the conflict and only 19% optimistic.

Thousands of people have been killed across the Middle East since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February, official figures show, with the vast majority coming from Iran and Lebanon.

President Trump is set to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the White House on Tuesday.

News.title: Boy, 16, charged with murder after Luton stabbing
News.content:
A 16-year-old boy has been charged with murder after the fatal stabbing of a 17-year-old boy in Luton on Friday, police have said.

Four other teenagers have been arrested on suspicion of murder relating to the same incident.

Officers were called to reports of violent disorder in Kingsway Recreation Ground at about 18:30 on Friday, where police said a number of teenagers were seen carrying large knives.

The 17-year-old was taken to hospital with multiple stab wounds but was pronounced dead shortly after. He has not been identified.

Following the stabbing, two teenage boys, a 16-year-old and a 17-year-old, were initially arrested on suspicion of violent disorder, before later being arrested on suspicion of murder.

Police said on Sunday the 16-year-old has since been charged with murder and has been remanded in custody.

Bedfordshire Police said the 17-year-old also arrested on Friday on suspicion of murder was being treated in hospital for serious injuries.

A further three boys, all 17, have been arrested on suspicion of murder, violent disorder and carrying a weapon, police said.

Det Ch Insp Nick Gardener appealed for anyone who was in the area and may have witnessed events leading up to the disorder to get in touch.

"Our officers are continuing to carry out additional high-visibility patrols, and we are continuing to engage with local members of the public.

"We would also like to remind the public not to share any distressing videos or images as this can be concerning for families involved, but also form a vital part of the police investigation," he added.

Zanib Raja, a councillor for the Biscot Ward in Luton, has also asked people not to share alleged videos of the incident online.

In a statement on Facebook, she said: "A tragic incident took place today in Kingsway Park, a place many of us grew up in, played in, and built memories in.

"A place that should be safe for families, children, and every resident of our town. Instead, a man lost his life in broad daylight. A family has been shattered. Luton is hurting."

Raja urged the community to come together.

News.title: Would you choose £50,000 over the chance of £1m?
News.content:
You have the choice of instantly receiving Â£50,000 or flipping a coin for a 50/50 chance of Â£1m.

Which would you choose?

The vast majority decide on taking the Â£50k, according to a survey of thousands of people by YouGov. Women voted 82% in favour of the guaranteed cash.

The poll has sparked a debate about why Brits appear more risk-averse than people in the US.

So why are the results so clear-cut, and what are the financial and psychological factors at play?

Sadly, there is little chance of ever having such a choice, but there are some interesting lessons for how we manage our money nonetheless.

News.title: Teen charged over record crossing on 'mega dinghy'
News.content:
A teenager charged over a small boat Channel crossing was allegedly piloting a "mega dinghy" carrying a record 165 migrants from France to England, the National Crime Agency has said.

Sudanese national Chan Mathok Atak, 19, is accused of endangering another during a journey by sea to the UK on Thursday and is due to appear at Margate Magistrates' Court on Monday.

The number on the dinghy broke the previous record from July, when 128 crossed the Channel from France on one vessel.

According to Home Office figures, more than 13,000 arrivals have been recorded in 2026, which is 45% lower than this time in 2025 and down 18% on the same period in 2024.

Border Security Command was pictured towing a dinghy - estimated to be about the same size as a standard bus at 13m (42ft) long - when it arrived in Dover in Kent on Thursday afternoon.

Home Office figures showed 366 people arrived after crossing in three boats on Thursday during warm, sunny weather and calm conditions at sea.

On Wednesday, 172 people made the journey in three boats, bringing an end to an 11-day hiatus because of windy conditions in the Channel.

Refugee charity Care4Calais said the crossing route was becoming "more and more dangerous" because of the increasing number of people in each boat.

News.title: 'Antisemitism felt relentless' - Jewish students on life at UK universities
News.content:
Like many campuses across the UK, Cardiff University has seen pro-Palestine protests in recent years and Oliver said he believed some behaviour he witnessed crossed the line from criticism of Israel into antisemitism.

Holding Jewish people responsible for the actions of the Israeli government is a form of antisemitism, according to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance.

"That first year was absolutely terrifying," he said.

"You go home and think, 'do I carry on? Do I try to go to the next day?'"

Oliver said he stopped speaking Hebrew outside his home, and hid his Star of David pendant when on campus.

Over the following three years, Oliver said the antisemitic abuse he experienced at university became "relentless".

"I've been in clubs [or] just wandering around the uni and you hear these conversations and you see pamphlets being handed around where it's literally saying that your belief and your history is fake," he said.

"I've been at house parties where, when someone's found out I'm Jewish they started calling me Netanyahu behind my back.

"Like you found out my religion and you've decided I'm a bad person."

Oliver said when he had reported antisemitic incidents that had happened to him and others, he had felt they had been often "swept under the rug" by the university.

Although he said some positive action had been taken, he feels more needs to be done.

Cardiff University said it was sorry that "any student felt unsafe" on campus and that it adopts a "zero-tolerance approach to harassment and discrimination of all kinds".

It said there was no place for antisemitism or hatred at the university and they have "robust procedures" in place for investigating allegations of antisemitism. Where it is found, the university said appropriate action would be taken.

It said it had reached out to the university's Jewish Society and reminded students to report incidents to them.

News.title: It's me, Cathy – thousands pay tribute to Kate Bush classic
News.content:
The sun may be hiding behind grey clouds, but for hundreds of people in flowing red dresses dancing on Yorkshire moorland it'll take more than a threat of rain to dampen their spirits.

This is BrontÃ« country, after all, so it's fitting that it's also perfect BrontÃ« weather.

The group, swaying in unison, have come together to re-create the music video for Kate Bush's 1978 song Wuthering Heights, inspired by Emily BrontÃ«'s novel.

Every year, thousands of people around the world don red robes â and in some cases long black wigs â for The Most Wuthering Heights Day Ever.

Events have previously taken place in places such as Sydney, Copenhagen, Berlin, Folkestone and Preston.

This particular "Mass Wuther" perhaps has an even stronger claim than most â it's held on Penistone Hill, not far from the famous BrontÃ« parsonage in Haworth, in the Pennines.

From the field on a clear day can be seen the ruined farmhouse of Top Withens, believed to be the inspiration for the titular farmhouse of BrontÃ«'s novel.

News.title: Iran's 'sabre-rattling' should not intimidate UK, Wes Streeting says
News.content:
When asked if Iran had the capability to attack the UK, Streeting said: "I think we shouldn't put too much stock in the sabre-rattling of Iran, and we certainly shouldn't be intimidated by what the regime has said this week".

He also repeated the UK's position from the outset of the US war against Iran saying "we have not joined and will not join offensive US military action in Iran.

"That's an area where we have not agreed with the United States, but when it comes to securing maritime freedom and free commercial shipping in the straight Hormuz, that's where we are absolutely aligned".

Streeting said he is to meet with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth in the coming week after "kicking around" ideas for ways "to bring the countries together" and had been "delighted" to speak to Hegseth by phone already.

He also said that the UK is ready to lead a naval mission to help remove mines from the Strait of Hormuz "when the conditions are right".

Securing safe shipping routes through the area was important because of the impact the crisis is having on energy prices and the cost of living, he added.

Streeting also dismissed a Russian warship's recent live-firing exercise in the English Channel as "performative" but added it was a "reminder of the frankly unsafe and unprofessional way in which they have been conducting themselves".

Branding the Channel incident "irresponsible", Streeting said Russia posed a threat to UK security, adding that the public does not see "the enormous efforts that take place every day to counter Russian aggression".

News.title: Family tributes to four men who died in crash
News.content:
The families of four men who died after a car hit a lamp-post on Merseyside have paid tribute to them.

The black Seat Cupra had been travelling from Liverpool towards Knowsley, before it came off the road and crashed on Liverpool Road, Huyton, just before 02:00 BST on Friday.

Jack Diggle, 23, Benjamin Dooley, 23, Andrew Roberts, 24, and Craig Shackleton-Brady, 26, all died at the scene, Merseyside Police said.

Officers are continuing to appeal for information about what happened.

The families of all four men released their tributes together through police.

Jack Diggle's mum said: "Jack was kind, quiet, thoughtful and loving. He adored his family, and we loved him with all our hearts.

"Jack was blessed with a wonderful group of friends, many of whom had been by his side for most of his life.

"He loved playing football with them and was a proud Everton supporter.

"Jack and I went out for a meal together on Thursday. It was such a lovely time, just mother and son, enjoying each other's company. Little did I know that it would be the last time we would spend together.

"Our Jack, our gentle giant, we love you beyond words and will love you forever. Rest peacefully, son."

News.title: Water returns to Gatwick Airport after major outage
News.content:
Gatwick Airport says its water supply has returned after passengers faced long queues for toilets and closed restaurants and bars after a major supply outage.

Both terminals at the UK's second busiest airport lost running water on Sunday morning after a power failure at a treatment works that serves the area.

People told the BBC of confusion and frustration as all bars and restaurants were shut, some were left with nowhere to sit and waits built up outside toilets.

SES Water, the company that supplies the airport, said earlier the power outage was fixed, with Gatwick reporting on Sunday night that water had returned to "the vast majority of the London Gatwick campus".

The water company, which also supplies parts of Kent, Surrey and south London, said complications caused by a power outage at Bough Beech treatment works meant some customers had experienced low water pressure or a temporary loss of supply.

A spokesperson had earlier confirmed that Gatwick Airport was affected.

On Sunday afternoon, SES Water said its treatment works were back up and running, but later added it would take time for the network to fully return to normal as it had been "a highly unusual and complex issue".

"We want to reiterate that our teams are working as quickly as they possibly can and we are grateful for everyone's patience," the spokesperson added.

Gatwick apologised and said staff had been handing out bottled water.

A spokesperson added: "Our staff are on hand to support passengers and provide assistance where needed, some restaurant partners have opened to provide additional seating."

Gatwick said additional teams had been deployed across both terminals to support passengers.

The airport added there had been no flight cancellations as a result of the supply issues and that it was working closely with SES Water to minimise the impact.

"Our teams are working hard to reopen toilets and other facilities as quickly and safely as possible," a spokesperson said.

News.title: Another UK heatwave looms after cooler end to weekend
News.content:
Sunday will be a cooler day for the whole of the UK as temperatures fall widely by a couple of degrees.

A few locations will finally mark the end to their third heatwave of the year, including Usk in Monmouthshire and Exeter in Devon.

Both places are forecast to see temperatures drop beneath the heatwave threshold for the first time in 21 consecutive days.

Temperatures will largely be in the mid-20s Celsius for the south-east of the UK and in the mid-teens Celsius further north.

For many, the relief from the heat will be short-lived as high pressure is set to build close to the south of the UK next week.

This will stall rain-bearing weather fronts and any wet weather will become confined to northern and western areas - especially north-west Scotland.

In southern parts of the UK, temperatures look set to climb once again.

Tapping into the heat over the near continent, the UK is likely to enter another heatwave, with temperatures in England and Wales forecast to peak around 25-32C for much of next week.

Yellow heat health alerts will come into effect for Yorkshire and Humber, the West and East Midlands, the East of England, London, south-east and south-west, at 9:00 BST on 28 July 2026 and last until 9:00 BST on 31 July.

The UKHSA warns that heat is expected to cause minor impacts for health and social care services, with an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

News.title: Man charged with two attempted rapes
News.content:
A man has been charged with two counts of attempted rape in Rochdale.

Harvey Symes, 23, is due to appear before Manchester and Salford Magistrates' Court on Monday, Greater Manchester Police said.

The force added that he has also been charged with threats to kill.

It follows an investigation after two women reported being attacked in Broadfield Park and Milnrow Park in the town on Saturday morning.
