Long before dawn breaks over Indonesia ’s largest landfill, Nur Wencih joins thousands of waste pickers climbing mountains of garbage, searching for anything they can sell.

The 35-year-old widow has worked at the site on Jakarta’s eastern edge for two decades, following her parents, who still earn a living there. The Bantargebang landfill has paid for food and rent while helping her two teenage daughters living with a relative in a rural village. She hopes her daughters will never have to follow the same path.

Living alone in a rented room near the landfill, Wencih earns about 200,000 rupiah ($12) on a good day collecting discarded toys, cardboard and plastic bottles before bulldozers bury them beneath fresh waste. Occasionally, she finds gold jewelry.

“It feels like hitting a jackpot,” Wencih said while taking a break from the sweltering July heat.

But those lucky finds, and perhaps her livelihood, may soon become far rarer.

Beginning Aug. 1, Indonesia plans to start transforming the site from open dumping to a more controlled system as part of a national waste management plan. The government last month announced it will shut down open-dumping operations at 343 of Indonesia’s 550 disposal sites, requiring them to transition to controlled or sanitary landfill systems and gradually accept only garbage that cannot be recycled or composted, such as diapers, dirty paper towels and stickers.

Meanwhile, residents are being asked to set aside organic waste and recyclables for separate processing, a practice many households have never been taught to do on a large scale.

Dudi Gardesi Asikin, head of Jakarta’s Environment Agency, said the policy aims to improve environmental health, reduce pollution and curb emissions of methane generated by decomposing waste.

Methane is responsible for roughly one-third of global warming and traps more heat than carbon dioxide, making it a key focus of worldwide climate efforts. U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres, for example, is urging governments to sharply reduce methane emissions, calling it one of the fastest ways to slow global warming.

A landfill at the center of the methane debate

Researchers say Bantargebang emits more methane than nearly any other landfill in the world, placing it at the center of Indonesia’s waste management reforms.

Asikin said Bantargebang opened in 1989 as a sanitary landfill equipped to collect methane. Unlike open dumps, sanitary landfills also cover waste with soil.

But after a private-sector contract ended in 2016, the facility gradually drifted toward open dumping.

"What was never intended to be open dumping became full open dumping,” Asikin said.

Only two of the landfill’s original 12 methane extraction wells remain operational, Asikin said.

Under the new plan, parts of Bantargebang are already being covered with tarps, and officials hope to cover much more. Asikin estimated that covering the rest of the disposal area could cost as much as 200 billion rupiah ($12 million).

Uncertain future for waste pickers

Indonesia faces a dilemma as it attempts one of its biggest waste-management reforms in decades while also protecting the livelihoods of an estimated 600,000 waste pickers.

At Bantargebang alone, officials estimate more than 4,000 registered waste pickers work among trucks, excavators and mountains of garbage each day. The materials they recover are sorted and sold to a network of traders and recycling businesses that have grown around the landfill.

“What worries me most is how I will feed my family,” Wencih said of the new plan, while excavators behind her pushed fresh waste onto exposed slopes.

Asikin said the government wants to improve conditions for waste pickers, who already receive some workplace protections and healthcare through a national social security program.

He believes the new policy will eventually create safer formal jobs in recycling and composting.

“Today they are practically racing against our excavators to grab recyclable materials. It is extremely dangerous," he said.

Bunin, a 53-year-old neighborhood chief who lives nearby, said while the landfill causes pollution, it also creates business opportunities including rental housing and food stalls catering to waste pickers.

“The landfill not only brings negative impacts, there are also economic benefits,” said Bunin, who like many Indonesians uses a single name.

A landfill at its limits

Covering roughly 110 hectares (272 acres), Bantargebang has grown into a human-made mountain reaching as high as 60 meters (196 feet), roughly the height of a 20-story building. About 7,500 tons of waste arrive daily from the capital city.

“The waste people produce does not disappear. It is gathered in one place and has become a mountain," said Agung Pujo Winarko, who heads the facility.

A collapse triggered by heavy rain in Bantargebang in March killed seven people, underscoring the risks posed by the landfill’s sheer scale.

“This situation is extremely urgent,” Winarko said. “Its carrying capacity is reaching, or even exceeding, its limits.”

Satellite data analyzed by UCLA’s STOP Methane initiative ranked Bantargebang in 2025 as the world’s second-largest landfill methane emitter after a site in Argentina.

Evan George from UCLA’s Emmett Institute on Climate Change and the Environment said reducing organic waste entering landfills could lower emissions, but that existing landfills will still require decades of monitoring and gas collection.

Changing Jakarta’s throwaway culture

Under the new approach, Jakarta residents are expected to separate food scraps and other organic waste from recyclables and residual trash before collection. New refuse-derived fuel plants are also part of the plan.

“What we are doing is somewhat revolutionary," Asikin said. "For decades, people were never asked to separate their waste.”

But many households are only beginning to learn the system, raising questions about whether enough public education has taken place.

“All we know is to throw the trash in the bin, not to sort it,” said Rukasih Wanti, a Central Jakarta resident. “The new rule is confusing us. It’s inconvenient, creates extra work and wastes our time."

Asikin said multiple government institutions, including education and health ministries, are supporting the efforts.

Environmental advocates say new recycling and composting infrastructure is also needed. The transition is daunting because government data shows only about one-quarter of Indonesia’s daily waste is currently handled by formal systems, with the remainder dumped, burned or otherwise unmanaged.

David Sutasurya, executive director of the environmental organization YPBB, said about half of Jakarta’s waste is compostable and another 30% recyclable, meaning up to 80% could be kept out of landfills.

“We delayed transforming our waste-management system for too long, and only realized the problem when landfills were already close to full,” Sutasurya said.

In a West Jakarta neighborhood, Monica T. Anggriani has spent more than a decade persuading neighbors to separate household waste, building a community waste bank that now processes about one ton of organic waste daily through composting, maggot cultivation and urban farming.

“Our generation was never taught to separate waste,” Anggriani said. “If we don’t start now, nothing will change in the future.”

___

Associated Press writer Jennifer McDermott in Providence, Rhode Island, contributed to this report.

Two people were hospitalized and multiple people injured after a car crash involving a self-driving Waymo in Los Angeles.

The two-vehicle accident took place at around 5.44am on Sunday in the Pico-Union area of the city near downtown, according to authorities.

The Los Angeles Fire Department said at least two people were taken to local hospitals and at least one other was treated and released at the scene, reported the Los Angeles Times.

Video and photos from the scene show debris scattered across the street.

Waymo told the outlet that in its view its car was not at fault for the accident.

Waymo carries out 500,000 weekly paid robotaxi trips across 10 U.S. cities as of March 2026 ( Getty Images )

The autonomous taxi firm stated that its Waymo car was driving at 27mph on Venice Blvd when the other vehicle, a blue sedan it says was traveling at between 47mph and 50mph, hit a pedestrian outside a crosswalk, swerved across the road and hit the Waymo.

”The safety of our riders and other road users is our top priority,” spokesperson Ethan Teicher said. “We are coordinating with first responders and are grateful for their quick response.”

Waymo carries out 500,000 weekly paid robotaxi trips across 10 U.S. cities as of March 2026, according to data analysis by TechCrunch.

The Independent has contacted Waymo for comment.

A congressional Democrat has doubled down on her demand that first son Barron Trump appear before the House oversight committee — saying he's a "full-blown adult" who should have to testify about rape suspects Andrew and Tristan Tate.

"There have long been ties between the Tates and the Trump family," Rep. Yassamin Ansari of Arizona told MeidasTouch podcaster Ben Meiselas. "It is reported that Barron Trump played a key role in facilitating, especially during the 2024 campaign, the relationship between the Tate brothers and the campaign."

"And, you know, Andrew Tate was very publicly supportive of Donald Trump," she added during the conversation posted online Saturday.

Ansari also concurred when Meiselas called Barron Trump, who turned 20 in March, a "grown-up," notwithstanding how Meiselas described the president as likening his youngest offspring to first lady Melania Trump's "little boy."

"Absolutely, I could not agree more," Ansari said. "Barron Trump is an adult. He is a full-blown adult, and he is very influential in the Trump White House orbit."

open image in gallery Barron Trump is a ‘full-blown adult’ who should have to testify about rape suspects Andrew and Tristan Tate, says Democratic Rep. Yassamin Ansari of ArizonaA ( Getty )

The White House didn't immediately respond to a Sunday inquiry from The Independent.

Last week, Ansari called on House oversight committee Chairman James Comer, a Kentucky Republican, to "swiftly open an investigation into the Tate brothers’ coordination and extensive relationships with members of the president’s orbit, including his son, Barron Trump.”

Her move came after 39-year-old Andrew Tate, a self-described misogynist and leading influencer in the online "manosphere," and brother Tristan Tate, 38, were arrested July 18 in Miami.

The U.S. Marshals Service took them into custody as British prosecutors said they were seeking to have them extradited to face charges of raping and trafficking women from 2010 to 2017.

The Tates deny any wrongdoing, and a lawyer representing them in the U.S. has called the U.K. charges "filth and slander," and predicted they "will walk free" following American court proceedings.

open image in gallery Ansari has called for a congressional probe ‘into the Tate brothers’ coordination and extensive relationships with members of the president’s orbit, including his son, Barron Trump’ ( MeidasTouch/YouTube )

The brothers were both ordered held without bond following a July 20 court hearing, but a series of first-person statements were posted on Andrew Tate's X account Sunday.

"England invented a MeToo from 20 years ago and I now languish in an American maximum security jail as a political prisoner. A shame," one statement said.

Another said, "There is no question of my innocence, especially amongst the British public, who have lost all faith in their judicial system and sent me thousands of letters."

It also compared Andrew Tate to WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and Donald Trump, saying they'd both "suffered the same" and asking "why are ancient MeToo allegations so against politically influential people taken seriously? Especially when they only appear once convenient."

open image in gallery The Tates face extradition to Britain, where they’re accused of raping and trafficking women from 2010 to 2017 ( Getty )

The Tates, who hold dual British and American citizenship, were previously arrested in Romania in 2022 on charges of human trafficking and forming a criminal organization to sexually exploit women.

The charges remain pending, but the brothers were allowed to leave the country in February 2025 and flew to Fort Lauderdale, Florida, on a private jet.

The BBC reported that their travel ban was lifted after several high-level White House officials took an interest in their case but that it was unclear what role, if any, the Trump administration played in the decision.

Trump has said he didn't know anything about the matter, and White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Thursday that the president wouldn't prevent the Tates from being extradited to Britain.

Oil prices eased in early trading Sunday, falling further from a two-month high set last week, after the United States and Iran refrained from launching military strikes in the Persian Gulf for a second straight day.

The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil to be delivered in September dropped 4.9% to $92.02 shortly after trading resumed. The decline followed a 3.9% drop on Friday.

Brent crude, the international standard, briefly hit $102 a barrel last week. That was $30 more than the most actively traded contract in the Brent market was going for early in the month, and the highest it had been since May.

Oil prices surged this month because of increased fighting in the Middle East and worries a return to all-out war would further slow the global flow of crude.

The ability of tankers to pass safely through the Strait of Hormuz has been the central concern for the oil market since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in late February. The narrow strip of water off Iran’s coast is the route through which a fifth of the world’s oil typically leaves the Persian Gulf and heads to customers worldwide, and the conflict has largely halted shipping traffic.

Oil producers have since searched for alternative routes, but those are under pressure too. Last week, attacks hit Saudi oil tankers that were using the Red Sea to leave the region. When less oil is available for customers to buy, the price goes up and fuel prices do as well.

In the United States, the average price for a gallon of regular gasoline on Sunday was $4.11, up from $3.90 a month ago and just $3.15 a year ago, according to motor club AAA.

If oil prices stay elevated, it could lead to higher prices for every product that gets shipped, trucked or flown around the world, including groceries. Although the U.S. economy continues to grow, the ongoing conflict with Iran has dragged consumer confidence in it lower.

The reacceleration of oil prices this month took place just as inflation had begun to slow more than economists expected. Now, traders believe inflation pressures have grown enough that they’re betting on a 36% chance the Federal Reserve will hike its main interest rate at an upcoming meeting, according to data from CME Group.

Higher interest rates would help keep a lid on inflation, but they could also slow the economy by making it more expensive for all kinds of Americans and businesses to borrow.

Long-term U.S. mortgage rates have already hit their highest levels in nearly a year, for example, chilling the housing industry. And more expensive borrowing could slow the boom in building artificial-intelligence data centers, which have become a big engine for the U.S. economy's growth.

While oil prices have given back some of their big July gains, much uncertainty still remains.

The price for a barrel of benchmark U.S. oil to be delivered in September fell 5.6% to $84.34 on Sunday. It dropped 3.1% on Friday.

In the oil market, traders are buying and selling contracts for barrels of oil to be delivered many months in the future. The price for a barrel of Brent crude to be delivered in October, which is now the most actively traded part of the market, fell 4.6% to $87.48.

News.content:

A New Jersey man was arrested after a 2-year-old boy overdosed on cocaine while allegedly in his care at the Jersey Shore.

Alexander Moles was charged after the youngster fell ill in North Wildwood on July 20, suffering from difficulty breathing.

Prosecutors say that firefighters were called to Moles’ vehicle, stopped at an intersection, after they received a report of a sick boy.

“EMS administered two doses of Naloxone nasal spray (NARCAN), to which the child responded to, and transported the two-year-old to Cooper University Hospital Cape Regional for further medical attention,” the Cape May County Prosecutor’s Office said.

“Preliminary blood tests of the two-year-old male were also positive for cocaine.”

Alexander Moles arrested after 2-year-old boy in his care overdoses on cocaine ( Cape May County Jail )

Moles, of Ringwood, New Jersey, faces charges of child endangerment and possession of cocaine, among others.

Investigators say that Moles, 39, was on vacation at a property in Wildwood at the time of the incident.

Court documents obtained by New Jersey 101.5 state that Moles was staying at a rental property with a woman and other children.

The documents state that he was responsible for the children while the woman took a shower. When she returned, she found that the boy was “sleepy”. Moles allegedly called her on his way to the hospital, saying that the child was falling asleep and the woman called 911.

Investigators say that during a search of the property, they found pieces of a pill, several tinfoil packets labeled “tapentadol hydrochloride”, and a clear plastic bag containing a white powdery substance, the outlet reported.

Moles was booked at Cape May Correctional Facility and released following a detention hearing on July 24, officials said.

Former US president Barack Obama is to tour the UK this autumn to speak about “what comes next for America”.

The 64-year-old will appear at events titled An Evening With President Barack Obama in Belfast, Glasgow and Manchester.

That follows shows at The O2 in London and Dublin’s Arena in 2025.

Mr Obama served as the 44th president of the US from 2009 to 2017. He was the country’s first Black president and its only one to date.

He will appear at The O2 in Belfast on 13 October, Glasgow’s Ovo Hydro on 14 October and Manchester’s Co-op Live on 15 October.

Guest moderators for the live interview shows are yet to be announced.

open image in gallery Barack Obama will appear in Belfast, Glasgow and Manchester this autumn ( AP )

Organisers said that Mr Obama will speak about “what comes next for America, and for all of us”.

Robin Sherry, founder and chief executive of organiser Seat Unique, said: “Following the phenomenal response to last year’s events, we are delighted to bring three new opportunities for fans to experience An Evening With President Barack Obama.”

Mr Obama was interviewed by British TV historian David Olusoga at The O2 in London in September.

During that talk, he lashed out at Donald Trump for “violence against the truth”, following the US president’s rogue declaration that painkiller Tylenol is linked with autism.

Mr Obama said that the unproven claims “undermine public health”.

open image in gallery Barack Obama and his wife Michelle signed a deal with Netflix to produce content for the streaming platform ( Getty )

“We have the spectacle of my successor making broad claims around certain drugs and autism that have been continuously disproved,” he told a 14,000-strong audience.

“All of that is violence against the truth.”

After his two-term presidency ended in 2017, Mr Obama and his wife, Michelle, signed a deal with Netflix to produce documentaries, series and features for the streaming platform under their Higher Ground Productions company.

That deal has since ended, with Mr Obama saying he and Michelle are in the process of “transitioning to a more independent [company] where we can work with a bunch of different studios”.

In 2022, Mr Obama won the Emmy for best narrator for his work on the Netflix documentary series Our Great National Parks.

He has also won Grammy Awards for his audiobook readings of two of his memoirs: The Audacity Of Hope and Dreams From My Father.

The former president, who was born in Hawaii, also hosted a 2021 podcast called Renegades: Born In The USA, alongside rock singer Bruce Springsteen, which also resulted in a book.

Tickets for the UK shows will go on sale on Friday 31 July at 10am from Myticket.co.uk and SeatUnique.com, with 100 tickets set aside for charitable organisations.

Location may be firmly at the top of many home buyers’ minds – but those searching for a property could potentially save significant sums by looking next door to pricey postcodes – according to a major bank.

Lloyds compared higher value postcodes in different parts of the UK with what it found to be the least costly neighbouring postcodes sitting next to them.

According to Lloyds’ analysis, homes in these neighbouring areas cost 28% less on average, but in many places the gap is significantly wider.

In the North East of England, Lloyds found that in the postcode of NE26, encompassing the seaside town of Whitley Bay, the average price was £304,022.

Next door in NE24, which takes in the town of Blyth, the average price of a home was £162,075 – £141,947 or 47% less than in neighbouring NE26.

Amanda Bryden, head of mortgages at Lloyds, said: “It’s easy to focus on the ‘must-have’ locations when you’re searching for a home, but this research highlights just how much value can sit right next door.

“Of course, neighbouring areas aren’t always directly comparable and each will have its own distinctive character, housing stock and local appeal.

“But in many parts of the country, looking just beyond the most sought-after postcodes can reveal more affordable options while still keeping buyers close to jobs, transport links, amenities and the communities that matter to them.

“For first-time buyers in particular, a small shift in location could make a big difference – not just in getting on the ladder, but in what kind of property is within reach.”

Lloyds said that in London, NW3 is among the city’s most expensive postcodes, covering locations such as Hampstead and Belsize Park. The average house price there was £778,767.

News.title: Lando Norris comes in from the cold with dominant Hungarian GP victory
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Community spirit

News.content:
Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

Kick-off is at 12.30pm.

News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

Sports.title: Jamie Gittens says £117m Morgan Rogers can win Chelsea the league – even if it pushes him further from starting XI
Sports.content:
MORGAN ROGERS’ British record move can drive Chelsea to win titles – according to the man trying to keep him out of the team.

Jamie Gittens is working back from a hamstring injury which curtailed a frustrating first season for the Blues, so perhaps the last thing he needed was a new £117million signing to compete with.



However, the winger has welcomed the addition of England star Rogers and feels the entire club has been boosted by his arrival alongside new boss Xabi Alonso.

Gittens, who made five England Under-21 appearances alongside Rogers, was training in front of 4,500 fans in Sydney as he and his teammates kickstarted their tour of Australia and Asia yesterday.



Rogers, on holiday after the World Cup, will not join up with Alonso’s squad until they return to London next month, but his move from Aston Villa – confirmed last week – has already sent ripples through the squad.

Gittens said: “We want to win everything – that is our ambition, to win the Premier League, the FA Cup and win anything that we’re in.

“Bringing in a player like Morgan will hopefully raise the bar to win titles. He’s a top player. That’s all I can say. He’s just an amazing player.



“Our quality is there, for sure, as a team we have individuals on the pitch who can do amazing things but we have to try and put that together.

“The squad is very competitive. We have to keep working hard and showing what we’re made of.

“Everyone is very positive, looking forward to the new season and to be better and to succeed, which is the main thing.”

Gittens had experience of facing Alonso’s title-winning Bayer Leverkusen side with Borussia Dortmund, from whom he joined Chelsea last year.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

While he only lost to them once in five appearances, a 3-2 defeat in which he scored, the winger says they were a challenging side to face and is delighted to now be working under the Spaniard – who was heavily involved in training down under.

He added: “That was hard! Because of the system, I’d say. It was a back three as well. They had Florian Wirtz, they had Jeremie Frimpong and, Amine Adli when we came off the bench sometimes, they had Piero Hincapie. Granit Xhaka as well. They were a real team.

“He [Alonso] was obviously a top player so for him to come in and teach us is the best thing for us.

“A World class midfielder, he’s probably the best to ever do it. He’s a very nice guy. He talks to us individually, speaks to us about what we can improve on, what we can do better. As a player, that’s all you want.



“He’s told me to keep being positive, to keep on taking on players, to keep on creating chances and to keep on pushing myself to the maximum.”

And how about being on the end of a pin-point Alonso cross in training? Gittens added: “It’s amazing, really. He does have a bit of an aura because he was a top player back in the day and obviously a top coach.”

Gittens himself is confident the energy of Alonso arriving alongside big signings can carry him to a much better season than last year.

The English winger arrived from Dortmund for £48.5m but scored just once in 27 appearances before a hamstring injury ended his season in February.



Gittens has been working every day over the summer, training solo on holiday in Portugal and Marbella to get ready for this season and noting down his objectives for a much better year.

He has started pre-season well, scoring in two behind closed doors friendlies against Crawley and Bromley before departing for the tour.

There is now a determination to show Blues fans exactly what he can do.

He added: “It was hard, because this was the first muscle injury I’ve had. I’ve never had hamstring injuries before.



“It was a challenge at the start, but I’m better now so I feel more confident.

“I’m feeling much better, more confident now my body is better, the hamstrings are good, so I’m just waiting for the season to start.

“I have set myself some objectives, individually, that I will keep to myself.

“This is such a big club. I want to succeed here. I need to show people what I can do. I’ll keep working hard. I’ve shown glimpses, I would say. Small bits. But this season will be a good season.”

Sports.title: Fury as EIGHT ‘greedy’ Prem clubs including Chelsea and Tottenham hike price of replica footie shirts to as high as £90
Sports.content:
EIGHT Premier League clubs — including Chelsea and Tottenham — have increased the price of their replica footie shirts.

Tens of thousands of fans now face forking out up to £90 to back their teams when the new ­season kicks off next month.



Spurs supporters must pay £90 for a replica adult first-team shirt, up £5 from last season. Chelsea has also hiked the price of a shirt by £5 to £89.99.

The biggest price rises, £10 each, are Sunderland and promoted Coventry City — from £60 to £70.



Ipswich Town has hiked prices by £6, or ten per cent, to £65

Leeds, Bournemouth and Hull shirts are all up in price by £5.

The average price of a basic adult shirt has now reached £77.20.

Ten clubs charge £80 or more for a shirt.

Brentford’s kit has a two year-cycle – the only Premier League club to do so — in a bid to keep them affordable.

Fans can also pay more to get names, numbers and badges added

Tottenham’s kids’ shirts are also the most expensive, at £70.

Coventry City children’s shirts are up by 25 per cent to £60.



Consumer expert Scott Dixon warned: “We see this year in, year out, and it smacks of blatant greed and an own goal that could backfire.

“These kits are ­overpriced by anyone’s standards and will leave many fans priced out.

“Fans deserve better. Clubs should be making it easier for the next generation of supporters to feel part of their club, not pricing them out.”

Sports.title: Arsenal will have to smash contract record to secure £400,000-week Vinicius Jr transfer from Real Madrid
Sports.content:
ARSENAL will have to break their own contract record to land Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr by offering him the highest wages in the club’s history.

The Gunners have launched an audacious bid to land Vinicius, 26, as they look to retain their Premier League title and go up an extra level by winning their first ever Champions League.



The North Londoners have turned their attention to the star forward, whose contract at Real runs out in 2027 and he has yet to agree fresh terms on his whopping £400,000-week deal.

But Arsenal would have to splash the cash to buy the Brazil international from Real, with new manager Jose Mourinho unwilling to part with the team’s biggest names.



The Prem champs would also have to at least match Vinicius’ Madrid salary if they hope to complete this massive transfer coup.

That means Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta would have to revert to extravagant contracts within his squad.



That was something Arteta eradicated upon his first year in charge at the Emirates back in 2019, when he swiftly axed the likes of Mesut Ozil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, who earned north of £350,000 per week.

However, Bukayo Saka recently put pen to paper on improved terms, which see him bagging about £365,000 per week.

That might soon become the norm, as the Spanish tactician wants to hold onto the key players that led to Arsenal’s first Premier League title in 22 years last season.

Arteta could also do with some improvement up front with the likes of Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli linked with exits after Leandro Trossard’s departure, which led to Christos Tzolis’ arrival.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

That is why Arsenal have been linked with Paris Saint-Germain ace Bradley Barcola as well, with his price tag currently in the region of £140m.

Barcola, 23, has also been linked with Liverpool but neither Premier League giant has made a serious bid.

This comes after Arsenal refused to meet Aston Villa’s £117m asking price for Morgan Rogers, who ultimately moved to rivals Chelsea on a British record transfer.

Sports.title: England DENIED automatic Euro 2028 spot for hosting – despite Argentina qualifying for World Cup by staging one match
Sports.content:
ENGLAND have to qualify for Euro 2028 despite being co-hosts – unlike Argentina at the next World Cup.

With millions of fans signing a petition to have the 2022 Qatar winners BANNED from future tournaments, they are furious to know a place in four years is already guaranteed.



And that comes with Lionel Scaloni’s side only hosting ONE game.

Spain, Portugal and Morocco are the 2030 World Cup hosts and have been given automatic berths.



But more controversially, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay have all been given places by virtue of hosting only their countries’ opening matches in the centenary edition.

England, however – who will welcome countries from across Europe for the 24 team Euros – are not in the hat for their own tournament just yet.



Games will be played across Wembley, the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Etihad, Everton‘s Hill Dickinson, St James’ Park, and Villa Park.

International tournament hosts are usually granted immediate entry into tournaments, like USA, Canada, and Mexico were for this summer‘s World Cup.

But new Uefa qualifying rules mean England will go into one of 12 groups of four or five sides along with all 50 other nations for Euro 2028, and won’t get the same degree of special treatment.

They will be kept apart from Scotland, Wales, and Republic of Ireland, who will also be hosting matches.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And all group winners go through automatically, as well as eight of the best runners up.

That is still only 20 of the 24 spots taken up, though, with two reserved for hosts in case they DO NOT qualify via the groups.

This means that if any two of the other hosts DO get through, England will be guaranteed a place no matter what they do as they will have a reserved space to themselves.

Although failing to get in via finishing top or second would raise serious questions.

And if three or four of hosts fail to qualify through the groups then only the top two highest ranked ones would get the designated host space.



England, again, are among the best in the world so will have a spot almost certainly theirs.

But at a time where Argentina are drawing mass criticism for behaviour on and off the field, their first-class ticket to Spain, Portugal and Morocco has frustrated footie watchers.

Sports.title: Facebook co-founder ‘invited to join Liverpool ‘takeover’ with Jeff Bezos as ex-Premier League owner spearheads bid’
Sports.content:
A CO-FOUNDER of social media giant Facebook has been invited to join a consortium with hopes of buying a stake in Liverpool.

Reports emerged earlier this week that a group of wealthy individuals were feeling out the purchase of a portion of the iconic North West club.



Amazon founder and one of the world’s richest men Jeff Bezos was said to be among those pitched the idea.

And now, according to reports from Sky News, it seems he could be joined in the endeavour by Eduardo Saverin, one of the minds behind Facebook‘s early success.



The Brazilian-born businessman helped get the site up and running alongside fellow Harvard student Mark Zuckerberg in 2004.

He left the company acrimoniously years later, but continued to grow his fortune in other endeavours, such as venture capital firm B Capital.



Forbes ranked him as the 68th richest person on the planet earlier this year.

Saverin has reportedly been approached by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia, who is spearheading the bid.

Bhatia has experience with professional sports business, serving as a co-owner, and at times Chairman, of QPR since 2004.

But he resigned earlier this week after 18 seasons with the West London outfit.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The syndicate are believed to have hired advisers to put together a deal with current Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG).

It is not known how or if Singapore-based investor Saverin has responded to the offer, but he could certainly bring some financial muscle to the table.

And he could potentially team up with Bezos to really bolster the backing of the Anfield outfit, who are trying to put together a deal for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola.

FSG confirmed the approach in a statement to the Financial times, saying: “An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.”

Sports.title: Surprise new job for Cristiano Ronaldo as ex-Man Utd ace agrees to star in huge drama about UK football
Sports.content:
ACE Cristiano Ronaldo is behind a major drama series about football — and will even star in it.

The former Man United striker is an executive producer of the show about a fictional agent, played by Homeland star Damian Lewis.



Filming has already started, with British star Damian seen at the home of Barnet FC, in North West London.

Ronaldo, 41, will appear and executive produce — while a TV insider revealed his former Arsenal rival Thierry Henry, 48, will also feature on the show, called Day 1s.



They said: “It’s likely to spark a bidding war between the streamers.

“The sheer calibre of figures behind it, not to mention the cast, means it’s a prestige project — albeit a surprising one for Ronaldo as he crosses into making dramas.”



It will tell the fictional tale of a top football agent called Stanley Dalton, played by Homeland and Billions star Damian Lewis, 55.

It is based on a concept devised by another of the show’s executive producers, real-life agent Darren Dein, 52, who represents Henry.

The insider added: “After the World Cup, there’s a renewed international interest, particularly in the States, in British football. It’s one that’s been growing for some time with shows like Ted Lasso.

“But this isn’t a sitcom. It’s definitely a drama, with some comedic elements, and has some serious names backing it.”



The show will be made by the new UR•Marv Studios, which Ronaldo runs with top director Matthew Vaughn, and will also star British rapper Dave and newcomer Carlotta Banat.

Henry was recently pictured at work on the first day of filming at the football ground of Barnet FC, in North West London.

Vaughn, who directed films including Kingsman and Kick-Ass, formed UR•Marv earlier this year, with the mission statement of disrupting the “conventional” movie-making market.



At the time, he said: “Cristiano has created stories on the pitch that I could never have written, and I look forward to creating inspiring movies with him.”

Ronaldo said: “This is an exciting chapter for me, as I look ahead to new ventures.” The ace, who has more than one billion social media followers, scored three goals for Portugal at the World Cup and still captains Saudi side Al-Nassr.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford told to release 'almighty statement' to save Man Utd career
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford told to release 'almighty statement' to save Man Utd career

Marcus Rashford saw a dream move to Barcelona fall through following his loan spell and the forward is expected to return to parent side Manchester United in the coming weeks

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is due to return to Manchester United after his World Cup commitments (Image: Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has been told to release an 'almighty statement' in a last-ditch effort to save his Manchester United career - but even that might only be enough for a bit-part role.

‌



The Red Devils academy graduate has fallen down the pecking order at Old Trafford over the past few years. He was initially sent out on loan to Aston Villa, before joining Barcelona on a season-long loan deal last term.

‌



The Spanish giants had an option to sign him permanently but decided against it in the end. That decision will see Rashford return to Manchester over the coming weeks, once he rounds off a holiday following his commitments with England at the World Cup.

‌



However, former England international Micky Gray believes Rashford needs to release a lengthy statement re-affirming his commitment to United.

Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit READ MORE :

Speaking on talkSPORT, he said: "There's a few things here. The most important one is, if Rashford has a future at Man United, he has to do an almighty statement of why he wants to be at Man United and what the reasons were to leave the club in the first place.

“I think that's a priority that he has to do. If he does stay then he's got to get used to being a bit-part player.

‌



"He's not first on the list; he's not going to be playing every week...[Bryan] Mbuemo, [Matheus] Cunha, [Benjamin] Sesko, Amad to name a few. They've caught up to and if not surpassed Rashford.

"Spain is not England. He did very well, but he can play at Barcelona at a different level to what he can at Man United. He can't deny that the Premier League is 100mph – he's going to have to get himself super fit in pre-season.

Rashford still has two years remaining on his contract with United, having only penned a new deal in 2023. He reportedly earns around £325,000 per week at Old Trafford.

It has been suggested that the Red Devils have set his price at around £40m despite Barcelona having had an option of £25m to sign him permanently in the summer.

Sports.title: Eduardo Saverin's huge net worth as Facebook co-founder approached over Liverpool investment
Sports.content:
Eduardo Saverin's huge net worth as Facebook co-founder approached over Liverpool investment

The transfer window is normally focused on the players on the pitch, but a recent report has suggested there may be a change coming in Liverpool's ownership

View 3 Images Eduardo Saverin has reportedly been approached to invest in Liverpool FC (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin has been approached by a consortium looking to purchase a share in Liverpool. Saverin, 44, is understood to have a net worth of around £24.3billion.

‌



Were he to involve himself in investing in the club, he would become the third wealthiest owner/co-owner in the Premier League. Only Newcastle United's Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund owners (£723.3bn) and Manchester City's 'City Football Group' bosses (£24.5bn) would boast a bigger net-worth than Saverin.

‌



In 2022, Saverin was part of a consortium which failed in an attempt to takeover Chelsea after Roman Abramovich was forced to sell the club.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

His £24.3bn net worth, according to Bloomberg Billionaires Index, would be more than welcome by the consortium looking to purchase a stake in the club. It's understood the syndicate could look to become the second-largest shareholder at Anfield.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos was also reported as another potential investor in the aforementioned consortium. At present, nothing has been decided in regards to Saverin being involved in the consortium.

‌



What is known is that it's currently being spearheaded by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal. The figure the consortium may look to purchase is understood to be around 30 per cent.

View 3 Images Eduardo Saverin has an enormous net worth (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group have been the majority stakeholders in Liverpool since 2010. A potential purchase could value the Reds at a whopping $6bn (£4.5bn) which would rank amongst the most lucrative deals in English football history.

‌



At present, Chelsea's takeover by the BlueCo consortium is the largest club purchase in English football history. When they won the bidding process at Stamford Bridge, the purported sale was worth around £4.25bn.

A spokesperson for FSG said last week: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

View 3 Images Jeff Bezos has also been approached over investing in Liverpool FC (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



In 2023, Dynasty Equity purchased a small stake which valued Liverpool at $4.5bn. This came one year after the club said they were open to a full sale of the club, which was confirmed in a statement.

At the time, they said: "FSG has frequently received expressions of interest from third parties seeking to become shareholders in Liverpool. FSG has said before that under the right terms and conditions, we would consider new shareholders if it was in the best interests of Liverpool as a club."

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit
Sports.content:
Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit

Jadon Sancho has been without a club since letting his deal at Old Trafford expire but it appears that the former Manchester United might not be out of work for much longer

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho could be Qatar-bound (Image: Getty Images)

Jadon Sancho has been handed the chance to complete a sensational move to Qatar after receiving a contract offer from Al-Rayyan. The former £85m man has been without a club since leaving Manchester United at the end of his contract.

‌



Sancho, 26, has been on the lookout for fresh employment since then but with little luck. But it appears he has now been offered a fresh chance to relaunch his career in the Middle East.

‌



According to the French outlet Foot Mercato, Qatari side Al-Rayyan have offered him a deal to sign him on a free transfer. They want the English wideman to be the leading face of their project to dominate football within the country.

‌



It is not revealed whether Sancho is tempted by the move as it stands, but either way, he appears to be closing in on a new club. The winger has also been linked with a return to German side Borussia Dortmund; Sancho having enjoyed a productive spell in the Bundesliga ahead of his big-money switch to Old Trafford.

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Since then, Sancho has had loan spells with his former club, Chelsea and Aston Villa. He has had mixed success with his temporary employers, Chelsea having chosen not to sign him permanently despite agreeing an obligation to buy clause with United.

He scored just five goals at Stamford Bridge, while Sancho only got on the scoresheet once during his time at Villa Park.

‌



Speaking last season, Dortmund managing director Lars Ricken suggested that they were interested in signing Sancho a third time. "We are currently looking at a lot of players and analysing them," Ricken said.

"We are assessing whether they can improve our team. We are doing the same with Jadon. Of course, we are looking for an offensive player who brings quality, can help us immediately, and doesn't require an unrealistic transfer fee.”

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho was last with Aston Villa where he won the Europa League (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Elsewhere, former Premier League boss Alan Pardew revealed what managers would be taking into consideration as they mull over a move for Sancho.

Speaking with talkSPORT, he said: "He hasn't really done enough to warrant a massive, massive contract like he was on at Man United, but he'll get a good move.

"When you get to the end of the season, it is an opportunity. You have to make some really tough calls on who to renegotiate with because obviously there's a value to the football club.

Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior transfer: Arsenal ready to break salary record to sign Real Madrid star

Arsenal are lining up a sensational swoop for Vinicius Junior and will offer the Real Madrid star a record-breaking salary in order to prise him away from the Bernabeu

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior currently earns a whopping £400,000 per week (Image: Bruno Penas/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

Arsenal would be willing to offer Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior the biggest contract in the club's history in order to complete a mega transfer deal. Vinicius, 26, has emerged as an ambitious target for Arsenal, who are closely monitoring developments regarding his uncertain future in Madrid.

‌



The winger has entered the final year of his contract with Real, who are due to pay him a lucrative loyalty bonus if he stays for the 2026-27 season. Los Blancos risk losing Vinicius on a free transfer next summer if they don't tie him down to a new deal.

‌



A report from the Telegraph states that his eye-watering salary of £400,000 per week wouldn't be a problem for Arsenal. In fact, Emirates chiefs would look to improve those figures in an effort to strengthen their chances of signing the Brazil international.

‌



Vinicius' prospective wages would dwarf those of Arsenal's current highest earner, Bukayo Saka, who signed up to a £365,000-a-week contract in February which will rise each season. The Gunners want to build on their Premier League title win and go one step further in the Champions League, having lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain in last season's final.

Left wing is a position which Mikel Arteta is keen to strengthen, having sold Leandro Trossard to Besiktas. Arsenal have already brought in Christos Tzolis, who can play on both sides of attack, for £34m but don't plan on stopping there.

‌



PSG's Bradley Barcola has been looked at in detail, with Premier League rivals Liverpool also interested in the Frenchman. However, both clubs have been quoted £145m.

Arsenal and Real haven't engaged in direct contact over Vinicius, who Jose Mourinho would be opposed to selling at the start of his second spell in Madrid. But concerns linger over how an attack containing both Vinicius and Kylian Mbappe can work at the highest level.

Sports.title: Chelsea sent strong transfer warning by Premier League boss after failed bid
Sports.content:
Chelsea sent strong transfer warning by Premier League boss after failed bid

Sunderland rejected an £8million bid from Chelsea earlier this summer for Granit Xhaka and Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris has now offered an update on the midfielder's future

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is overseeing his first transfer window as Chelsea boss (Image: Getty Images)

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris has confirmed Granit Xhaka will be going nowhere, weeks after turning down a move to Chelsea. The former Arsenal man was considering a sensational swithc Stamford Bridge earlier this summer.

‌



Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso was also keen on a deal that would have seen him reunited with the former Bayer Leverkusen star. But an agreement could not be found between the two clubs and Le Bris has announced that there is no chance of a revival in talks.

‌



Asked about Xhaka’s future after his side’s pre-season defeat to Liverpool, the Frenchman said: “No, this topic is closed.

‌



“He has been really clear about his future. He loves Sunderland, he wants to stay in Sunderland. He wants to make the future of Sunderland. He is a good captain. A great leader.”

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Le Bris’ comments come just weeks after Xhaka appeared to perform a U-turn about his future. Speaking during the World Cup, the Swiss midfielder said: "That's not my job [to talk about a potential move to Chelsea]. I have my management for that. I want to concentrate fully on the World Cup."

But just shortly after, he committed his future to the Black Cats. Xhaka said: "Sunderland has been my home since day one. We are all very happy. I've decided to stay where I am; the most important thing is family. I'm ready to make history with them."

‌



Xhaka, 33, only joined Sunderland last summer from Leverkusen, having helped the German side to the Bundesliga title. It also signalled his first return to the Premier League following a rollercoaster spell with Arsenal.

View 2 Images Granit Xhaka was the subject of a bid from Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Xhaka made 36 appearances and scored one goal for Sunderland across what was an impressive debut campaign at the Stadium of Light. His performances helped the club secure a spot in the Europa League for the forthcoming season.

‌



Sunderland’s summer window has been relatively low-key this term, having only signed Thomas Meunier on a free transfer. Asked if fans could expect any more business, Le Bris added: “It’s going to be quiet.

“Under the radar, right? Because I think we are working hard behind the scenes, and it's really important to be quiet because otherwise, it's a mess.

“And we are looking at probably a different transfer window if you compare with last season. We had to sign 14 new players. That won't be the case this year. We'll see what will happen.”

Sports.title: Federico Chiesa confirms Liverpool future stance and reveals new role under Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa confirms Liverpool future stance and reveals new role under Andoni Iraola

Federico Chiesa was tipped for the exit door under Arne Slot, but Andoni Iraola's appointment marks a fresh start for the Liverpool forward, who's being used in a new position in pre-season

View 2 Images Federico Chiesa wants to earn the trust of Andoni Iraola (Image: Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Liverpool star Federico Chiesa says that he isn't thinking about a transfer and has revealed that new manager Andoni Iraola wants him to play as a striker. Chiesa, 28, has only started two Premier League games since his £10million move from Juventus in 2024 and has frequently been linked with a move away.

‌



The forward wasn't trusted by former boss Arne Slot, who was sacked in May following a disappointing season, and wants to put a marker down in pre-season under Iraola. Chiesa got off to a good start by scoring in Liverpool's 4-2 victory over Sunderland in Nashville, and he helped set up another.

‌



Post-match, the Italian made it clear that wants to make a success of his career with Liverpool after a frustrating first couple of years, adding that he's set to play centrally under Iraola rather than on the wing. "Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool," Chiesa affirmed.

‌



"I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool. I don't know, it is difficult to say [if this is a fresh start].

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

"It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year. Maybe there have been too many fresh starts. But I don't care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager. Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best.

‌



"Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not. Of course, I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer decided to do so, he had his game plans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football.

"This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that. He put me striker today and he wants me there. The only conversations I've had [with Iraola] were about pressing and tactics."

Should Liverpool sell Federico Chiesa? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Federico Chiesa played - and scored - as a striker against Sunderland (Image: Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Chiesa feels a responsibility to make amends for Liverpool's 'lucky' fifth-place finish last season, as the Reds narrowly qualified for the Champions League on the final day. "Liverpool deserves more," the 28-year-old declared.

"Two years ago, we were Premier League champions. Last year, we almost went out of the Champions League spots. We were battling for fifth, which was enough at the time but as we know usually only four go in. We were lucky."

Sports.title: Wantaway Tottenham star emerges on Arsenal and Chelsea radar in transfer twist
Sports.content:
Wantaway Tottenham star emerges on Arsenal and Chelsea radar in transfer twist

Rarely do Premier League rivals look to do transfer business with each other, but it's been claimed Chelsea and Arsenal are eying one of Tottenham's biggest stars

Sports.title: Rising star Koivun holds off Scheffler to win on third PGA Tour start as a pro
Sports.content:
Jackson Koivun held off a charge from world No 1 Scottie Scheffler to win his first PGA Tour title in just his third start as a professional as he triumphed by three strokes at the 3M Open in Minnesota.

The 21-year-old's final-round, five-under 66 came after Scheffler - looking for his first title since the American Express back in January - applied the pressure with an eight-under 63 to post the clubhouse score at 22 under par.

Koivun had carved out a three-shot lead over Emiliano Grillo and Ben Kohles after round three following a stunning, bogeyless 10-under 61 that included two eagles and four birdies on an eight-under back nine.

Image: Scottie Scheffler's eight-under 63 came in vain on Sunday as he finished three shots adrift of Koivun

The youngster's Sunday was not as dramatic but he kept his cool to complete victory, securing the 3M Open scoring record of 25 under par in the process as he finished a blemish-free weekend with a par.

Koivun, who had made 10 starts as an amateur on the tour, turned professional after the US Open in June and missed the cut in his first event - the John Deere Classic - before finishing tied-10th at the Isco Championship.

He made 24 birdies, those two Saturday eagles and just three bogeys all week at TPC Twin Cities during a performance that hinted at an extremely bright future and also pushed him up 124 spots in the FedExCup standings to 70th, the final play-off berth with two regular events remaining.

Image: Koivun won his first PGA Tour title at the age of just 21

Koivun: Golf was love at first sight

He said afterwards: "I played a great round of golf. I definitely had some nerves coming down 18.

"I heard the crowd saying, 'Scottie's coming, Scottie's coming' but I just tried to blank that out and play the golf I knew I could. I was able to find some good putts down the stretch.

"I love this game, it's everything I do. It was love at first sight and I just want to say thanks to my parents for getting me into this and supporting me on my entire journey."

Image: Koivun made just three bogeys throughout the week, all in his second round

'Houdini chipper Koivun will make it to the top'

Sky Sports' Simon Holmes on Jackson Koivun:

"He is turbocharged and ready to perform immediately. He has presence in front of the camera and media. This guy is going to create a lot of fans.

"If you look at some of the talent th.at has come through that college system - Jordan Spieth, Collin Morikawa and Viktor Hovland - you'd say he is at least on a par with all of those players. But there is something in him that sets him apart from that group.

"Spieth had amazing putting but not a great driver. Morikawa, similar, amazing irons.

"With Koivun, you say driver, fantastic - he can play golf from the middle of the fairway. Iron control, amazing. Can he chip? Absolutely, he is a [Harry] Houdini.

"The best parts of his game are his putting and his mindset. He sees himself reaching the top of the pyramid - that is the outcome he expects.

"Let's see him make that journey. It's going to happen."

Sports.title: Craig Overton wins battle with brother Jamie in entertaining Hundred finish
Sports.content:
Craig Overton won his one-on-one battle with twin brother Jamie as Trent Rockets beat London Spirit by four wickets with two balls to spare in The Hundred.

Rockets needed 10 runs from the final five deliveries at Trent Bridge on Sunday night with Craig batting for the hosts and Jamie bowling for the visitors.

Craig (20no off six) earned bragging rights, and two points for his team, by top-edging Jamie for six over deep fine leg and then picking up successive twos to take Rockets to their target of 160, after Ben Duckett had spanked an excellent 75 off 47 balls up top.

Image: The Overton twins shake hands after Sunday evening's match at Trent Bridge

Craig Overton's six-two-two off his sibling had mirrored his efforts off Andrew Tye across the previous three deliveries with a maximum over long-on followed by a brace of two-run hauls, exploits that helped Rockets to a first win of 2026 and condemned Spirit to successive defeats.

Earlier in the game, Overton had caught and bowled Spirit opener Jonny Bairstow for a duck and also dismissed South African biffer Lhuan-dré Pretorius for 24.

Pretorius' compatriot Dewald Brevis top-scored with 39 from 24 balls in Spirit's 159-9, while captain Liam Livingstone contributed 33 off 24 deliveries.

Buttler blasts Super Giants to back-to-back wins

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch all of Jos Butler's sixes in Manchester Super Giants' win over Birmingham Phoenix

Elsewhere, Jos Buttler cracked 90 from 50 balls as Manchester Super Giants hammered Birmingham Phoenix by 87 runs to join Welsh Fire in winning their first two matches.

Buttler's knock at Emirates Old Trafford, which featured seven fours and five sixes and helped Super Giants post 187-5, was only 10 runs fewer than Phoenix managed as an entire team, with the visitors bundled out for 100 as Liam Dawson claimed 3-15.

The hosts backed up their narrow seven-run win over Spirit at Lord's on Thursday, while Phoenix slipped to a first loss having edged Rockets by 10 runs in a high-scoring clash at Edgbaston on Friday.

Image: Super Giants seamer Josh Tongue celebrates the wicket of Phoenix's Rehan Ahmed

Buttler was supported by Tom Moores' 39 not out off 17, which included five maximums, but Phoenix's batting never got going with skipper Donovan Ferreria (23) top-scoring.

England pacer Josh Tongue struck twice in two balls to rock Phoenix early, inflicting a golden duck on Rehan Ahmed, and the Midlanders never really recovered.

England quick Sonny Baker and Afghanistan spinner Noor Ahmad also bagged two wickets for Super Giants, who look to have an excellent all-round attack.

What is happening in The Hundred on Monday?

After the four-games-a-day set-up at the weekend, Monday sees a return to a single double-header with Southern Brave's women's side hosting MI London from 3pm before the men's sides square off from 6.30pm. Catch both fixtures live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: In-form Herbert breaks LIV Golf record with win in UK
Sports.content:
Australia's Lucas Herbert followed an impressive showing at last week's Open at Royal Birkdale with a record-setting victory at the LIV Golf UK event in Staffordshire.

Herbert, who finished tied for sixth in the final men's major of the year, four shots adrift of champion Ryan Fox, romped to the LIV trophy in Rocester with a score of 30 under par.

That was the lowest winning score since the circuit was established in 2022 and left the 30-year-old six strokes clear of Tyrrell Hatton and nine in front of Bryson DeChambeau.

Image: Herbert's win was his second on LIV in 2026, after May's event in Virginia

Herbert also set the LIV record for most birdies in a tournament (30) and most combined birdies and eagles (32) after a 10-under, blemish-free 62 on Sunday.

He had begun the event with an 11-under 61 that contained 10 birdies and an eagle and his worst round all week was a three-under 69 on Saturday.

Herbert shot an eight-under 62 in the second round of the Open earlier this month and said after his victory at Rocester, his second of the LIV season after triumphing in Virginia in May: "I just wanted to carry that into this week the best I could.

"It was good to play like that today when I was being pushed by two of the best players in the world."

Hatton carded a nine under 63 on Sunday and said: "I wanted to get off to a fast start, which I did, but unfortunately Lucas did as well.

"It would have been amazing to win in front of home fans, but I tried my best. Lucas was incredible this week."

Sports.title: Mayo win first All-Ireland title in 75 years as 'curse lifted'
Sports.content:
Mayo claimed a first All-Ireland Senior Football title for 75 years as they beat defending champions Kerry in a thrilling final at Croke Park.

Mayo had lost 11 finals in a row, two of which went to a replay, since their last title in 1951 but secured a 1-20 to 1-17 triumph in emotional scenes on Sunday.

Manager Andy Moran - who lost six finals in a row during his playing days with Mayo - guided the club to silverware in his first season in charge.

Captain Jack Coyne told the BBC after Mayo's fourth title overall: "This is the stuff of dreams. To every Mayo boy or girl around the world, dream big things.

"Everything is possible and we showed that today. The saying is keep the faith. We kept the faith. We're All-Ireland champions."

Legend has it that a curse was placed on Mayo back in 1951 when their homecoming celebrations after winning the title disrupted a funeral.
