Sports.title: “Disgraceful”: Wolff criticises “Teletubbies” at rival teams over blue flags delay | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff criticised engineers at rival teams for failing to react to blue flags during the Hungarian Grand Prix.

A system fault during the race meant the light panels stopped working and drivers were only shown blue flags manually. This caused problems for Andrea Kimi Antonelli when he was trying to catch Max Verstappen over the final laps while under pressure from Lewis Hamilton behind.

“The marshalling system was not functioning and cars in the back were defending on a Lewis and Kimi fight,” Wolff told Sky. “It’s just disgraceful from some of the Teletubbies engineers that sit on the pit walls of these teams not telling the drivers what’s happening behind.”

However some of the same drivers who delayed Antonelli had already held Verstappen up.

“It’s unacceptable how long that takes here with this car,” Verstappen told his race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase at one point. “Mate, what are they doing?”

After being held up by another car Versstappen exclaimed: “They should get a penalty. This is fucking ridiculous, these morons, my god.”

Wolff admitted he was “not happy about the whole situation” after the team left Hungary with third place for Antonelli and seventh for George Russell, who fell to the back of the field at the start after a problem with his engine.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We did a mistake on screwing George’s start,” said Wolff. “It’s just not acceptable and not good enough for us.”

Russell said there was “nothing I could do, unfortunately.”

“I was on the throttle, waiting, and then all of a sudden the engine was going all over the place. It was revving really high, really low.

“Right now we don’t know but it’s added to the list of things that has happened this first half of the year and pray things calm down in the second half.”

Sports.title: Sainz collision was “one of the dumbest things I’ve ever seen” – Piastri | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The stewards ruled Carlos Sainz Jnr was entirely to blame for the collision which cost Oscar Piastri the lead of the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Piastri was vying for the lead of the race with team mate Lando Norris when he tangled with Sainz while trying to lap the Williams. Sainz was preoccupied with his fight for position with Fernando Alonso

Although Piastri avoided spinning after the pair made contact at turn three, he lost time which allowed Norris to make his second pit stop and emerge ahead of his team mate.

The stewards handed Sainz a five-second time penalty for the collision. Although they considered some factors in mitigation they ruled Piastri was not to blame for the contact.

Sainz indicated he was unaware how close Piastri due to a problem with the flag marshalling system which occured during the race.

“The incident with Piastri could have been avoided with a bit better communication and a bit of bad luck with a [blind] angle in my mirror,” he said. “I just didn’t know he was there so I had no clue. He was lapping us and he was in my [blind] spot in the mirror.”

However Piastri said “that’s no excuse at all.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“That’s got to be one of the dumbest things I’ve ever seen on a race track,” he told Viaplay. “I don’t really care what excuse he gave.”

Williams team principal James Vowles said they should have done more to alert Sainz to the McLaren behind him. “We should have done a better job of warning him about Piastri,” he said. “We never want to interfere with the leaders, and we need to make sure we avoid that in future.”

Stewards’ verdict on Sainz for collision with Piastri

On lap 38, at the approach to turn three, car 55 [Sainz] was engaged in a battle with car 14 [Alonso]. The driver of car 55 had been informed by the team that blue flags were being shown due to the approach of car 81 [Piastri]. As car 81 attempted to overtake, contact occurred between cars 55 and 81. The stewards determined that the driver of car 55 was wholly responsible for the collision with car 81. While the standard penalty for causing a collision is a 10-second time penalty, the stewards identified a mitigating factor. At the point of the incident, the positioning of car 55 relative to the circuit and the other cars meant that car 81 was not visible to the driver of car 55 prior to the attempted overtake. Although the driver had been informed that car 81 was approaching, the stewards accepted that the limited visibility reduced the degree of culpability. Taking this mitigating circumstance into account, the stewards determined that a five-second time penalty, rather than the standard 10-second penalty, was appropriate.

Sports.title: Norris pounces on Piastri’s clash with Sainz to grab first win of 2026 | 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
Lando Norris claimed his first victory since winning the world championship in the Hungarian Grand Prix.

The McLaren driver capitalised on a clash between his team mate Oscar Piastri and a backmarker to regain the lead he lost at the start of the race.

Norris held his lead from pole position but immediately ran wide at turn two. That opened the door for Piastri, who started third, to dive by into the lead.

Piastri maintained the effective lead of the race after the drivers made their first pit stops. But Norris closed on his team mate during their second stint on hard tyres.

Norris urged McLaren to give him the opportunity to pit first but the team resisted, sticking to their policy of giving the leading car the first tyre change. They duly brought Piastri in for the second time on lap 34.

Piastri’s race went awry soon afterwards, however, when he caught Fernando Alonso and Carlos Sainz Jnr. The Williams driver was so preoccupied with trying to pass his rival he failed to notice Piastri poking his nose alongside into turn three. The pair made contact and only Piastri’s quick reactions kept him from spinning.

Norris’s pit crew pounced, swapping his tyres immediately and jumping one McLaren ahead of the other. That left only Andrea Kimi Antonelli between him and his first victory of 2026, and Norris easily breezed past.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

A final blow struck Piastri with 15 laps to go, when his gearbox failed. Norris took advantage of the subsequent Virtual Safety Car period to take a set of soft tyres for his final sprint to the flag.

When the race resumed Max Verstappen held second place on a worn set of soft tyres, pursued by Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton. The Ferrari driver overtook the Mercedes as he rejoined the track following a pit stop under the VSC, but after his team took a close look at the replay they told him to let Antonelli by to avoid a penalty.

Antonelli and Hamilton set off in pursuit of Verstappen but found progress difficult as they lapped a success of slower cars. Hamilton was further compromised when the stewards issued him a five-second time penalty for speeding in the pits.

The pair ran out of time to catch Verstappen, so Norris ran out the winner by 15 seconds. Verstappen prevailed in a spirited battle with Hamilton early in the race, re-passing his former championship rival after their first pit stops.

Antonelli took the final podium place, increasing his championship lead. Hamilton’s penalty dropped him to fifth behind. Charles Leclerc.

George Russell’s championship hopes suffered another blow as his car went into anti-stall at the start, dropping him to 20th place. He recovered to finish seventh after running out of time to catch Isack Hadjar.

Liam Lawson prevailed in a scrap with his team mate to take eighth place. Nico Hulkenberg also passed Arvid Lindblad as he finally claimed his first points finish of the season,

The only drivers to join Piastri in retirement were Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez, who both suffered technical failures on their Cadillacs.

Sports.title: Vladyslav Sirenko Knocks Out Otto Wallin With One Second Left
Sports.content:
The finish gave Sirenko (23-1, 20 KOs) a signature victory in his first appearance under the Zuffa Boxing banner. Wallin (28-4, 16 KOs) suffered one of the most devastating knockouts of his career.

For much of the fight, neither heavyweight appeared close to producing such a sudden ending. They traded willingly from the opening round, spending long stretches working at close range. Sirenko consistently targeted the body and often forced Wallin backward with his aggression.

Wallin, 35, relied on his experience to keep the fight competitive. The Swedish southpaw used subtle footwork to create punching angles, landed accurate counters, and gradually opened swelling beneath Sirenko’s right eye. His cleaner punching allowed him to bank several rounds as the bout reached the middle stages.

The pace remained high despite obvious fatigue setting in during the closing rounds. Sirenko continued pressing the action even after showing signs of exhaustion, while Wallin matched him with determined exchanges that kept the outcome in doubt entering the final minute.

With only a second remaining before the final bell, Sirenko uncorked a straight right that snapped Wallin’s head back before immediately following with a left hook. The combination landed flush and left Wallin unconscious as he crashed to the canvas, ending the contest without the need for a count.

The knockout instantly became one of the standout finishes of the year and capped a bout that had looked destined for the scorecards. Instead, Sirenko walked away with the highlight-reel finish, while Wallin left the ring receiving medical attention after the brutal final sequence.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson Needed Only 30 Seconds Against Marvis Frazier
Sports.content:
Despite the modest crowd in Glens Falls, ABC’s Wide World of Sports broadcast the fight nationwide. Tyson earned approximately $135,000 for the bout, well below Marvis Frazier’s reported $250,000 purse. It proved to be the last time Tyson made less money than his opponent.

There was no cautious opening. Tyson stormed across the ring behind his trademark pressure, clipped Frazier with a right hand, then trapped him near the corner. A pair of uppercuts followed. The second, a crushing right, left Frazier unconscious before he collapsed to the canvas without landing a meaningful punch.

Referee Joe Cortez immediately realized the fight was over. He halted his count at five after seeing Frazier was unresponsive, later remarking that he “could have counted to 20” because fighter safety came first.

Tyson later revealed he sensed hesitation from Frazier before the opening bell. He expected the fight to end quickly. Once the excitement faded, his attention turned to Frazier’s condition after the stoppage.

The victory became another milestone in Tyson’s unforgettable 1986 campaign. He returned less than a month later to stop José Ribalta, followed with another knockout over Alfonzo Ratliff, then demolished Trevor Berbick in November to become the youngest heavyweight champion in boxing history.

Marvis Frazier never regained his place among the heavyweight contenders. He boxed only three more times before retiring in 1988. Tyson’s 30-second destruction of Frazier remains the fastest knockout of his professional career. Four months later, he captured the heavyweight championship, making the victory one of the defining performances of his rise.

Sports.title: Spencer Brown Dismisses Anthony Joshua Victory: Tyson Fury Wins That Fight Comfortably
Sports.content:
“I was in shock. I was in a lot of shock,” Brown told Seconds Out. “Wait till he gets in with big Tyson Fury. That’s a different beast. He’s a different beast. That performance was an easy performance yesterday.”

Brown admitted he believed Joshua’s comeback bid had already ended after the opening round.

“Thought we’d lost the fight. It was all over. The dream was over. Thank God he got up and he did what he did,” said Spencer.

Brown’s view matched criticism from several figures in boxing who questioned Joshua’s display despite the knockout victory. Getting dropped twice by a late replacement left many wondering how Joshua would fare against elite opposition after returning from his lengthy layoff.

He believes Joshua’s struggles confirmed his view that Fury wins if the long-discussed British heavyweight fight finally happens. Instead of treating Joshua’s knockout as proof he has returned to top form, Brown saw a performance that Fury would handle comfortably.

Brown also rejected criticism that Fury looked sluggish during his own return, suggesting much of it came from Joshua supporters.

“The people criticizing him are Anthony Joshua fans, aren’t they? Simple. Social media. They criticize me, they’ll criticize you, they criticize everybody. That’s what it is,” said Brown.

Brown believes Joshua’s struggles confirmed his view that Fury wins if the long-discussed British heavyweight fight finally happens. Instead of treating Joshua’s knockout as proof he has returned to top form, Brown saw a performance that Fury would handle comfortably.

While Brown was quick to dismiss concerns over Tyson Fury’s own recent outing, the contrast on the canvas is hard to ignore. In his return against 46-year-old Mariusz Wach, Fury offered little of the fleet-footed brilliance that defined his victories over Wladimir Klitschko or Deontay Wilder. Looking slow, heavy, and visibly faded, Fury relied on raw size to wear down Wach over seven grueling rounds before forcing a clubbing stoppage.

The last eight years have exacted a heavy toll on the former champion. Brown may dismiss the sluggish display as simple social media blather, but Fury’s labor against an aging journeyman suggests time has caught up to both heavyweights, making any potential meeting far less predictable than his manager claims.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Should Face Yoenli Hernandez Next
Sports.content:
Yoenli is one of the best young middleweights in the sport. The unbeaten Cuban has combined his outstanding amateur pedigree with power, stopping nine of his first 10 opponents. He has looked like a future world champion from the start of his professional career, making him the ideal measuring stick for anyone with title ambitions at 160 pounds.

At 31, Tszyu doesn’t have the luxury of taking three or four tune-up fights before stepping into meaningful competition. If his goal is another world title, he’ll eventually have to beat fighters on Hernandez’s level or deal with champions like Carlos Adames. Defeating lower-ranked contenders first would do little to answer the questions surrounding his future in the division.

A victory over Hernandez would immediately establish Tszyu as a legitimate middleweight contender. It would erase much of the doubt created by his recent defeats and place him within striking distance of another title opportunity. Losing would provide an equally valuable answer by showing that the division’s bigger, stronger fighters present a hurdle he may not overcome.

Tszyu rebuilt momentum with his victory over Spence, but that win came against an opponent making his first appearance in nearly two years. Middleweight presents an entirely different challenge. Hernandez offers the type of test that reveals exactly where Tszyu belongs.

Instead of spending months collecting routine victories, Tszyu should take the direct route. If he wants to reinvent himself at middleweight, there may not be a better first opponent than Yoenli Hernandez.

Sports.title: Keyshawn Davis Sees Haney Win Changing Boxing
Sports.content:
When I stop Devin Haney it will be a new face of boxing.⭐️ — Keyshawn Davis (@KeyshawnDavis8) July 26, 2026

Bill Haney quickly fired back, placing the burden of making the fight back on Davis’s side.

“Stop ducking meetings with your manager and promoter; let’s get this deal done. ⭐️” Bill replied on X.

The public back-and-forth comes just ahead of Monday’s WBO purse bid if Haney’s side fails to reach an agreement with Keyshawn beforehand. Davis has repeatedly pushed for the fight, viewing it as the ultimate opportunity to claim a world title.

Stopping Haney would give Keyshawn, 27, the type of signature victory that every contender chases. It would also answer questions about how he compares against one of the sport’s best-known names.

Becoming boxing’s new face is another matter. Winning over fight fans across the U.K. alongside the American market requires real star power. Defeating Haney in a tactical chess match won’t instantly transform Davis into a global superstar. Haney is a defensive specialist lacking explosive power, whose recent performances against Brian Norman Jr. or Jose Ramirez failed to excite audiences.

Inside the ring, Keyshawn’s composure under fire remains a major issue. When opponents land solid shots, he sometimes loses his cool and resorts to wrestling tactics. Fans saw it against Miguel Madueno when the bout turned ugly, and again in his May rematch with Nahir Albright, where sheer frustration over holding led Keyshawn to execute an illegal body slam that cost him two points. That habit of losing his head and turning fights into dirty grappling matches turns off fight fans who expect disciplined brilliance from a star.

To earn true crossover stardom, Keyshawn needs more than a single win over a defensive champion. He would likely need to clear out the entire welterweight division, sweeping through marquee names like Ryan Garcia, Conor Benn, Rolly Romero, Teofimo Lopez, Richardson Hitchins, plus potential moving contenders like Andy Hiraoka and Ernesto Mercado.

If the fight gets finalized, Keyshawn will get his opportunity to back up his claim inside the ring, but proving he belongs at the top spot will require a far longer journey.

Bill Haney reacted to Keyshawn’s post from above, telling him to stop ducking his manager so they can make the fight.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua Admits He Never Expected First-Round Scare Against Prenga
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua admitted he never expected to find himself fighting through a first-round crisis after being dropped by Kristian Prenga on Saturday night in Jeddah. Instead of panicking, Joshua said he accepted the situation, tightened his defense, and trusted he would eventually wear his opponent down before scoring a second-round knockout.

“It’s not what you expect, honestly,” Joshua said to iFL TV. “One thing I’ve learned is these guys are starting fast. They’re not coming to box 12 rounds and see if they can outbox me. They’re coming to try and take my head off. “In the second round I said to myself, ‘I can do the same. What am I waiting 12 rounds to break them down for?’ I’ve got some power in my hands, so I might as well land some leather as well. I learned a lot in that moment.”

Joshua said he expected to build behind his jab before breaking Prenga down, but the first-round knockdown changed everything.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga vs. Steven Butler Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Results

Vladyslav Sirenko produced a dramatic finish by knocking out Otto Wallin with only seconds remaining in the 10th and final round of their heavyweight bout. Sirenko uncorked a right hand followed by a left hook that left Wallin unconscious, bringing an abrupt end to a closely contested fight. Wallin, 35, remained down after the knockout and was removed from the ring on a stretcher. The finish gave Sirenko (23-1, 20 KOs) a knockout victory over former world title challenger Otto Wallin.

Welterweight Emiliano Moreno earned an eight-round unanimous decision over Arnold Gonzalez in a competitive fight. Moreno (13-1, 7 KOs) built momentum after a closely contested start, landing the cleaner punches and applying steady pressure to take control over the second half of the fight. Gonzalez enjoyed success in spots, including a strong rally late in the seventh round, but he was unable to sustain it over the full distance. The judges scored the contest 79-73, 78-74, and 78-74 for Moreno, giving him a successful debut under the Zuffa Boxing banner.

Kashaun Davis outboxed Mihai Nistor over eight rounds to earn a unanimous decision in a clash between unbeaten heavyweight punchers. Davis used quick combinations and fast hands to control the action, while Nistor (8-1, 8 KOs) spent much of the fight trying to slow the pace by tying him up. An accidental head clash opened a cut over Nistor’s right eye, and he later lost a point for repeated holding in the fifth round. The judges scored it 80-71, 80-71, and 79-72 for Davis (12-0, 11 KOs), who picked up the first decision victory of his professional career.

Troy Nash remained unbeaten with an eight-round majority decision over Ethan Perez in a competitive featherweight matchup. Perez (8-1-1, 3 KO) applied steady pressure during the early rounds, but Nash (8-0-1, 1 KOs) answered with a sharp jab and composed boxing that allowed him to control many of the exchanges. Neither fighter was knocked down as both prospects boxed at a high pace through the final bell. The judges scored it 79-73, 79-73, and 76-76 for Nash, handing Perez the first loss of his professional career.

Dominique Francis boxed well early, but Andres Sosa shifted the fight in his favor after dropping him with a left hook in the third round of their eight-round super featherweight opener. Sosa kept coming forward, landing overhand shots plus steady body work that gradually wore Francis down over the second half of the contest. Francis rallied in the final round, looking for a late breakthrough, but Sosa answered back often enough to stay in control. The judges scored it 79-72, 78-73, and 77-73 for Sosa, handing Francis the first defeat of his professional career.

Sports.title: Gene Tunney Stops Tom Heeney, Retires Four Days Later
Sports.content:
The bout carried the NYSAC, NBA, and The Ring world heavyweight titles. Promoter Tex Rickard presented it as what many believed would be Tunney’s final appearance. Tunney weighed 192 pounds. Heeney came in at 203½ pounds. Jack Dempsey, whom Tunney had defeated twice, worked in Heeney’s corner in an effort to help the challenger dethrone his former rival.

A paid crowd of 43,191 attended, with thousands more admitted on complimentary tickets. The gate reached approximately $691,014.50, producing a net of about $521,422 after expenses. Tunney received a remarkable $525,000 purse, while Heeney earned $100,000. Motion picture rights generated another $20,000. Radio rights produced $15,000.

Referee Eddie Forbes officiated. Charles F. Mathison and Tom Flynn served as judges.

Heeney fought exactly as expected, charging forward in an effort to force exchanges at close range. Tunney relied on disciplined footwork. His steady left jab repeatedly disrupted the challenger before sharp counters landed cleanly. Much of the early action featured clinches as Heeney struggled to trap the champion along the ropes.

By the eighth round, Tunney had opened a damaging cut over Heeney’s left eye. The punishment increased in the 10th when a double jab followed by a chopping right hand dropped the challenger near the ropes. Heeney rose immediately. He kept pressing forward despite absorbing heavy punishment.

The finish came at 2:52 of the 11th round. Tunney unloaded another sustained attack, but Heeney refused to fall. Seeing the exhausted challenger taking unanswered punches, Forbes stepped between them and awarded Tunney a technical knockout victory.

The victory became the final chapter of one of boxing’s finest championship careers. Tunney retired as heavyweight champion. Later that year, The Ring magazine selected him as its inaugural Fighter of the Year for 1928. Heeney earned lasting respect for his determination, although the defeat effectively ended his pursuit of the world heavyweight title.

Ghana News.title: Tanzanian lecturer arrested over anti-government protests charged with terrorism
Ghana News.content:
A Tanzanian university lecturer who was arrested earlier this month over allegations of inciting anti-government protests has now been charged with terrorism.

Melkisedek Kaijage, who works at the University of Dodoma, had appeared at a magistrate's court to request bail after spending 15 days in police custody when the charges were changed.

He was among more than 130 people arrested over planned protests calling for democratic reforms and justice for those killed in a post-poll crackdown last year. The 7 July demonstrations were banned and did not take place.

The academic will now remain in custody until his case goes to trial as terrorism offences are generally not eligible for bail.

Kaijage, who teaches political science and public administration, was not asked to enter a plea at Thursday's hearing as his terrorism case can only be heard by a higher court.

He was arrested a day after the planned nationwide protests and initially charged with inciting people to join them.

The authorities had deployed security forces across major cities in the East African nation on 7 July and warned that they would act against anyone accused of inciting unrest.

Prosecutors now accuse Kaijage of threatening to burn public buildings as part of intimidation tactics.

Under Tanzanian law, offences such as recruiting for, facilitating, harbouring or supporting terrorists or terrorist groups carry severe penalties. Individuals convicted of these offences may face prison sentences ranging from 10 years to life imprisonment.

Gerald Shija, chairman of the University of Dodoma Academic Staff Association (Udomasa), said Kaijage had been transferred from police custody to Isanga Prison in the capital, Dodoma.

Colleagues have described him as a respected lecturer whose popularity stems from his teaching rather than political activism.

His case comes amid a broader crackdown by the authorities on opposition figures and activists critical of President Samia Suluhu Hassan.

Last month, the government suspended political rallies across the country until further notice, saying the move was necessary to maintain security.

During the widespread protests that followed the results of the 29 October 2025 election, 518 people died from "unnatural causes", including 197 who were shot dead, according to a commission of inquiry established by President Samia.

The scale of the violence shocked a country that had cultivated an image of calm, consensus and stability for nearly six decades.

President Samia was declared the winner the poll with 98% of the vote, a result the opposition dismissed as a "mockery" of democracy after her two main challengers were excluded.

At the time, the president said the election had been fair and transparent and blamed foreigners for the violence, saying it was part of a plot to overthrow her.

Ghana News.title: The notorious Cameroonian prison with its own record label
Ghana News.content:
New Bell - a notorious prison in Douala, Cameroon - is a city within a city.

The facility has its own "taxis" (inmates who whizz through congested courtyards on foot to hand deliver messages), its own law enforcement (burly prisoners who help stretched guards police the facility) and market (a string of stalls where convicts sell and buy goodies, like fried cassava and beignet pastries).

Basically, the occupants of New Bell have adapted the jail's slack laws to work for them. The clearest example of this spirit is Jail Time Records, an on-site music studio and label making mini stars out of the most talented prisoners.

Empereur, the feared leader of gangs inside and outside of the prison, has amassed 24,000 YouTube views with a music video filmed entirely in prison.

Songs from the inmates have gained fans from as far away as South Africa, the US and Argentina, while earlier this year Jail Time Records put on a huge concert for the prisoners in New Bell's courtyard.

"It's this instrument of resistance… where we can really share friendship, love and our voices can be heard," Steve Happi, the former inmate who co-founded Jail Time Records, tells the BBC's Talking Movies programme.

"We don't think anymore about the four walls - we find the freedom."

The Jail Time Records studio is rudimentary - a small, sweaty recording booth attached to a room inhabited by a solitary computer.

But it is also the site of great catharsis and creativity, as per a recent, acclaimed documentary named after the studio.

Directed by Happi and Italian artist Dione Roach, his Jail Time Records co-founder, it was filmed in New Bell over six years.

Last month it won three prizes, including best documentary feature, at New York's Tribeca film festival.

In the film, a prisoner named Stone raps into the studio's microphone: "Heart of stone, it's war. My senses shatter like broken glass.

"I'm closed and tight like a cell door. No solid ground I slip like a fish."

Stone (R), a former soldier in the presidential guard, raps and produces music with Jail Time Records

Stone, who used to be a soldier in Cameroon's presidential guard, was sentenced to 10 years in New Bell for robbery and illegal possession of firearms. He insists he is not guilty.

The film captures him trying - often unsuccessfully - to reach his young daughter Maira on the phone.

"It's been a long time. She needs to hear my voice from time to time, so she doesn't forget about her father," he says in a voice message to a family member, after failing to get through to Maira yet again.

The music video for Heart of Stone is a typical Jail Time Records affair. The production value is high, storytelling is captivating and hordes of fellow inmates get involved as actors and crew.

"The music that comes out of there is amazing," says Taika Waititi, the New Zealand Oscar-winning director who, with his wife, the singer Rita Ora, served as an executive producer for the Jail Time Records documentary.

"Just in terms of the power of art in relation to redemption and what that can mean to someone who, you know, some of these people are in prison for life. I think having an outlet is an incredibly powerful and humane thing," he says.

Jail Time Records was founded in 2018, when Roach volunteered for a non-profit organisation running events inside New Bell.

During a dance class for the prisoners, a crew of rappers took over the microphone and began freestyling. Impressed by their performance, she asked the prison authorities for permission to start up a studio.

The powers that be were receptive and so Roach enlisted Happi to run the studio as a producer and sound engineer.

The inmates attempt to secure an optimal view for the Jail Time Records concert in February

According to Happi, he ended up in New Bell following a family argument over what should be done with his late father's body.

Amid the dispute, his aunt, a high court judge, allegedly arranged for him to be thrown into jail for killing his father. He was acquitted of the crime two years later, Jail Time Records says.

In 2022, Happi, Roach and the prisoners released an album named Jail Time Vol 1. As is customary for Jail Time Records' music, half the profit from the album's sale went to the artists and the rest was reinvested into the label.

The studio's survival is paramount to many of the artists, especially given New Bell's bitter environment.

In 2022, Human Rights Watch reported that New Bell was housing 4,700 prisoners within its crumbling walls - four times its capacity.

The prison's packed population, along with its unsanitary conditions, enabled cholera to spread rapidly during an outbreak four years ago, rights groups have said. At least six inmates died from the disease.

New Bell also has a reputation for violence. In 2008, guards shot 16 inmates dead during an attempted breakout.

Prisoners also attack and intimidate each other - the documentary captures Empereur, who is serving 10 years for multiple crimes, shaking down a bewildered young inmate for a necklace chain and some flip-flops.

Asked if the Jail Time Records project might glorify Empereur, the son of a traditional Douala chief, and other criminals who have committed violent crimes, Roach tells the BBC: "The process we're doing is a rehabilitation process, basically.

"We enter the prison without any judgment and it's the only way we can really approach this kind of work.

"Music, as with any creative process, is also a way of self-discovery... coming to terms with things you've done and hopefully changing for the better".

Former New Bell prisoner Steve Happi (R) directed the documentary with Dione Roach (C) and Taika Waititi (L) was an executive producers

The prison authorities appear to share this view.

"They were really welcoming of the project. Cameroon is a super musical country… everyone loves music," Happi says, adding that the head of the prison attended this year's concert and proceeded to dance with the performers.

With official support, Jail Time Records has been able to flourish, offering opportunities to more prisoners, including those in New Bell's women's wing.

Jeje, Jail Time Records' first female artist, made her debut in 2022 with the brooding Afrobeats song Show Me The Way.

"Nobody show me the way, nobody show me the way, I did it all alone," sings Jeje, who was jailed after stealing money and running away from an allegedly abusive uncle.

Jeje recorded her Afrobeats song in the yard of New Bell's women's wing

As well as working with the women's wing, Jail Time Records have expanded their project outside New Bell and Cameroon.

Roach and Happi set up a studio 1,000 miles (1,600km) away in 2023, in the central prison of Burkina Faso's capital city, Ouagadougou.

Jail Time Records hopes it can replicate the success of the original New Bell studio, with its accompanying label, music video production arm and now, award-winning documentary.

The film ends with an "in memoriam" sequence; a tribute to six prisoners who died while the Jail Time Records project has been running.

New Bell may appear to be endlessly bleak, but according to Happi, music provides the inmates with a "lantern for a brighter future".

"Before that, they had the stubborn mentality: it's them against the world," he says.

"They feel now important - they feel like they have a place in the society."

Ghana News.title: Would you pay $58.5m to live in this iconic New York building?
Ghana News.content:
The Flatiron Building - with its unique triangular shape, narrow prow, ornamental columns and intricate decorative details - has been one of the most recognisable structures in New York City for more than a century.

But for the last seven years, the Flatiron has been shrouded in scaffolding, its Beaux-Arts exterior hidden from throngs of tourists who came to view it.

It has been undergoing a large-scale renovation, both internal and external, from an awkwardly laid-out office building into ultra-luxury apartments - with new units going for up to $58.5m (£43.9m). Only 21 residences currently on the public market or under contract in New York City are priced higher, with the top spot occupied by a $128m (£96.1m) condo off Central Park, according to data compiled by Manhattan Miami Real Estate.

Now, with its transformation nearly complete, the Flatiron is ready for its next - and most extravagant - phase of life.

For over 120 years, the building has been a testament to architectural ingenuity, and while that history is highlighted in its redevelopment, the building is also becoming a symbol of just how expensive the city's luxury apartments can get.

The Flatiron Building, seen here in 2023, was covered in dark scaffolding for years

A dramatic impact on the neighbourhood

The Flatiron Building's renaissance harkens back to when it was originally built.

Completed in 1902, the building was an architectural marvel with a pioneering steel-frame construction making it one of the city's first skyscrapers.

Designed by architect Daniel Burnham to fit onto a wedge-shaped plot of land at the intersection of Broadway and Fifth Avenue, it was initially dubbed "Burnham's Folly" because locals feared that its height and thinness would cause it to blow over.

The Flatiron Building under construction in 1902

For years, tourists flocked to a small triangular park out front to snap a selfie with the full structure behind them.

But after the scaffolding went up and the pandemic hit, the park saw a slight drop in visitors, said James Mettham, president of Flatiron NoMad Partnership, a business improvement district that operates the park space.

As the scaffolding has come down, he says the visitors have returned.

"People are coming back to get their pictures, and then in turn will go shop at the local retail, and all the great food and beverage that's around here," Mettham said.

"So getting it back in all of its glory to complement everything that's been going on around it is really important."

Originally built to house the Fuller Company, a Chicago construction firm, the 24-storey, 94m (307ft) tall building has had many occupants, including clothing and toy companies, magazines, and publishing houses.

The Flatiron Building photographed upon its completion in 1902

But in its 100-plus-year history, it was always an office space – until now.

After the last office tenants, Macmillan Publishing, moved out in 2019, scaffolding went up and it sat vacant through years of ownership disputes.

The building's current owners – the Brodsky Organization, GFP Real Estate, and the Sorgente Group - began renovations in 2023, after announcing they would convert it into high-end condos.

Once completed, the building will have 36 open-concept apartments – some half-floor and some full-floor units – ranging from $11m (£8.3m) for three-bedroom units to $58.5m (£43.9m) for a full-floor five-bedroom residence with a balcony,which is currently in contract.

A rendering of what a unit on the 20th floor will look like once completed

Amenities also are being added to the building's basement and common spaces, including a 18m (60 ft) pool, billiards room and piano lounge, and wellness centre.

New residents are expected to start moving in in the coming months, the owners say. All units and amenities are expected to be finished in early 2027.

A rendering of the mezzanine game room, one of several amenities that will be offered to new residents

In this view of a model unit on the north side of the 12th floor, the narrowest point of the triangular room is around 1.8m (6ft) across

The other side of the 12th floor north unit is seen here, with an open-concept kitchen and more rectangular shape

How do you make a triangular residence desirable?

When New York design firm Studio Sofield was hired to reimagine the building's interior, it had to address the problem of the building's previous life as an office space, co-founder William Sofield said.

Another big hurdle came with the building's shape. How do you subdivide a triangle – just 1.8m (6ft) across at its narrowest point - into luxury apartments worthy of a multimillion-dollar price tag?

But the triangle itself – along with its history, architectural ingenuity, and novelty – is exactly the point.

"It wasn't about changing anything that makes the building so special and beloved to New Yorkers," Thomas Brodsky, partner at the Brodsky Organization, told the BBC.

"The layouts and the proportions and views really came directly from the architecture rather than from how we generally would start planning a building from the ground up."

Originally designed to evoke a classic Greek column, the structure's limestone, brick and terra-cotta exterior features ornamentation including lion heads, wreaths, eagles, and faces.

Beyer Blinder Belle, lead developer on the building's exterior, enlisted a speciality manufacturer in California to replicate and restore thousands of terra-cotta pieces from the facade, reinstalling each by hand.

The building's windows, totalling over 1,000, also needed to be replaced – dating back to the 1970s, they were too heavy, hard to open, and not energy efficient.

The new ones are thick enough to block the bustling noise of surrounding streets, offering silence in units that's uncharacteristic of New York City apartments.

The windows, seen here in the 12th floor model unit on the south side, throughout the building have been replaced

Steel beams holding up the skyscraper are exposed in various corners of residential units - an homage to what made the original building so innovative. In the 12th-floor model unit, the steel framework has even been turned into closet shelving.

The scaffolding is expected to be fully removed by the end of summer.

When the restored exterior is unveiled for the first time in seven years and illuminated for the first time ever, everyone will get to appreciate its beauty, said Mettham.

"Whether it's functioning as an office for one of the world's largest publishing companies, or it happens to have really expensive condos," he said, sitting in a small park at the building's prow, "the exterior, and what we see from these spaces right here, we share in that. We are all part of that."

A rendering of what the building will look like when all the scaffolding is down and it is fully illuminated for the first time

Old menus, a hidden balcony and a wooden revolving door

The redevelopment led to some unexpected discoveries.

While removing sheetrock during demolition, workers found remnants of a balcony at the triangular point on the 20th floor, identical to an existing balcony one floor above.

"It's kind of the hidden jewel in the building that nobody knew about," said Carlos Cardoso, partner at Beyer Blinder Belle.

That balcony, overlooking the treetops of Madison Square Park and the length of Broadway, has now been restored.

Construction workers have been working to restore the newly discovered balcony

Going through the building's cavernous basement – which once housed two restaurants – crews found fragments of a wooden, revolving door dating back to the 1910s. That door was so damaged that it couldn't be salvaged, Cardoso said, so it was replicated.

The building's developers have found other ways to incorporate the building's past into its new life.

Steel balustrades from an old staircase found in the basement were repurposed as legs for apartments' bathroom sinks. Mosaic tile lettering on the floors marking each apartment number is a recreation of the originals.

The steel balustrades on the bathroom vanities were taken from an old staircase

A rendering of a private entry vestibule, with historic mosaic tiling on the floor

Other artifacts found in the basement – tools, a piano, original restaurant menus, shoes, s, shirts, lights, and buckets – will be displayed in glass cases in the lobby, giving modern dwellers a glimpse of Flatiron's past.

A "nearly forgotten" historic streetlamp that once stood outside on 23rd Street has been reimagined as a chandelier in the lobby, Sofield said.

Sofield said he was inspired to recreate this streetlamp, seen here in 1895, in a new chandelier for the residential lobby

Paneling from one of the building's original restaurants was recreated in the trim of the new pool. Vintage planters and awnings as well as antique light fixtures and window curtains are being incorporated into the street fronts.

And the building's entire facade – with its unique form and intricate detailing - will be showcased with new lights, allowing passersby to admire it at night.

"Unlike many buildings in New York, the Flatiron is seen in the round," Sofield said. "All sides are extraordinary."

Ghana News.title: Ryan Gosling to join Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ghost Rider
Ghana News.content:
Ryan Gosling will join the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) as the titular character in a new Ghost Rider film, the media franchise has announced.

Speaking during the surprise announcement at San Diego Comic-Con on Saturday, Gosling said it is a character he has "wanted to play for a very long time".

The film is due to be released in 2028, and will be the third about the motorcycle-riding anti-hero. It will follow the 2007 film of the same name starring Nicolas Cage, and its follow-up, 2011's Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance.

At a separate event at the convention, the actor Ryan Reynolds made a surprise appearance as the Marvel character Deadpool, who he has played in a series of films.

This year's convention has ushered in a number of Marvel updates for fans, including an exclusive trailer that was shown of the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday film and an announcement that Black Panther 3 would be released in 2028.

Johnny Depp made a special appearance, as did Rick Moranis when he announced a sequel to the 1987 parody film Spaceballs.

Before making the big reveal about Gosling's addition to Marvel, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige said on stage that he had often been asked when Gosling would join the MCU.

Shortly after, the lights turned off. When they returned, the actor appeared on stage to cheers from screaming fans.

Speaking about the role, Gosling, a three-time Oscar nominee, said: "Wow, is this really happening?"

He has previously spoken about his desire to take on the role. Appearing on Josh Horowitz's Happy Sad Confused podcast in March, the Hail Mary and La La Land star confirmed he was in discussions with Marvel.

Ghost Rider is the anti-hero identity of motorcycle stuntman Johnny Blaze.

The character's story begins when he becomes bound to the Spirit of Vengeance Zarathos after making a deal with villain Mephisto to spare his surrogate father, giving him superpowers.

The film will be directed by Shawn Levy, who Gosling described as the "only" director for the project.

Levy has previously directed Deadpool & Wolverine in the MCU, and is currently working with Gosling on Star Wars: Starfighter, which is due to be released next year.

Levy told the crowd that he and Gosling spent a lot of their downtime on set daydreaming about Ghost Rider and swapping ideas.

The director said: "As Ryan started talking about his vision for this character, we started riffing, and I finally said, 'bro, let's ride', so guys, we'll see you in 2028."

The other famous Ryan - Reynolds - made his own appearance at a panel for the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday film.

Ryan Reynolds appears as Deadpool at San Diego Comic Con.

Dressed in a grey version of Deadpool's suit, he asked teasing questions of celebrity panellists like Robert Downey Jr and Paul Rudd.

"When do you start filming?" Reynolds asked the cast.

Downey Jr shot back, "It's in the can, bro, look around you. Did you bump your head?"

Ghana News.title: Berlin Pride attack suspect shot and killed during police operation
Ghana News.content:
The man suspected of carrying out what authorities say was likely an "Islamist terror attack" at Berlin Pride has been shot and killed by police.

Officers opened fire when Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old German citizen with Lebanese heritage, rushed at them with a knife in Spandau, a western borough of Berlin.

It brought an end to a massive manhunt that was launched after a white van was driven into a crowd of people near Tiergarten park just before 22:00 (local time) on Saturday evening, killing one woman and injuring at least 29 others.

Police say following the ramming, several people were injured in a stabbing attack.

Investigators at the scene in Tiergarten park on Sunday

Speaking to reporters on Sunday, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said evidence pointed to it being an "Islamist terror attack".

"We are dealing with a suspected perpetrator, who had previously drawn attention to himself through a high volume of criminal offences, radicalisation and affiliation with the Islamist scene," Dobrindt said.

A statement released by the Berlin public prosecutor's office revealed further details about Ballout's criminal history.

In May 2025, prosecutors said he travelled via Turkey to Lebanon, with the intention of joining the Islamic State group (IS) in Syria. While in Lebanon, he allegedly made contact with several individuals he believed were members of IS.

He was arrested in Lebanon in July 2025 and sentenced to three months in prison for incitement to religious and sectarian conflict.

Then, in November 2025, he returned to Germany, where he was arrested at Berlin Brandenburg Airport and held in pre-trial detention.

In May this year, he was sentenced to one year and 10 months in prison for "preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state". The decision was deferred for six months and he was placed under the supervision of a parole officer.

He was previously convicted of assault and robbery in 2022, and of robbing a victim of headphones in 2020.

Abdul Ballout was shot and killed in a police operation on Sunday afternoon

Dobrindt said Germany's threat level would be raised following the attack, while other states were also being briefed about the attack and advised to review their security measures for major events.

On Sunday, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited the scene of the attack in Tiergarten park.

He later spoke outside a church service that paid tribute to victims, where he pledged to "defend the freedom and openness of our lives".

"These extremists have no place in our society," he said, adding that Germany would not allow the "poison of terrorism" to affect its society.

Berlin police have said people were hit on Ahornsteig street, which is a long path stretching across the Tiergarten park, largely in a forested area.

Meanwhile, German media say those injured in the attack are no longer in a life-threatening condition.

Saturday's attack shattered the joy and revelry of Berlin's Christopher Street Day, where hundreds of thousands spill onto the city streets for one of Europe's most famous Pride events.

Christopher Street Day commemorates the first known uprising among the LGBT community in New York City in 1969 at the Stonewall Inn, which is located on Christopher Street.

A clean-up event due to take place at Tiergarten park and a breakfast market scheduled for Sunday morning were both cancelled following the attack.

Later in the day, some members of the LGBT community returned to the iconic Brandenburg Gate for an impromptu vigil.

Speakers condemned extremism in all its manifestations, but they also criticised the government for a lack of support, singling out recent budget cuts for queer organisations.

Armin Duenhoelter from Wolfsburg, who works as a drag artist, was backstage at the main stage when the attack happened.

He told Agency France-Presse that he was still shocked but vowed to be back for next year's pride celebration.

"We won't let it beat us down," he said.

Ghana News.title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump ‘if right for Britain’
Ghana News.content:
Andy Burnham says he would be prepared to call out Donald Trump to defend Britain's "national interest before anything else" if it is the right thing to do, in his first major interview as prime minister.

Speaking exclusively to the BBC, Burnham said he had had a good first exchange with Trump, finding him to be "really warm".

But asked twice if he would trust the US president, he did not say, answering, "it's a changing world, isn't it, and you just obviously have to call things as they develop".

In the interview, to be broadcast in full on Monday, he said: "I can't at any point say that I won't take a different opinion from him [Trump], that I will need to voice a different idea that is right for Britain."

Burnham said: "My strength is remaining close to people, close to the public, that will not change as prime minister."

Asked if he would call out Trump if it was the right thing, he said, "of course", going on to say: "You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly."

Burnham also said he had had "concern" about the president starting the conflict with Iran, and he "wouldn't hold back from saying what I think is right".

Responding to Burnham's comments, Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: "Clearly, the US is a long-standing ally. We need to have good relations with them, but if they do something we disagree with, we should honestly say so."

The prime minister would not commit to a date when the government would spend 3% of GDP on defence. His Chancellor, John Healey, resigned from the previous government, saying that unless a commitment was made to spend that amount by 2030, the country would not be safe.

But Burnham said: "I appointed my new chancellor very aware of what he had said about the critical importance of defence spending and the position that he had taken about that.

"The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that's the thing that's right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year."

Asked again specifically about the commitment to increase defence spending to 3% of GDP, he said: "We've got to work out the way of doing that."

Burnham, for the first time, explicitly dismissed the idea of an early general election before 2029, saying: "I'm going to rule it out... I don't think people want it." He said his focus instead was on "getting the country back where it should be".

Philp said the Conservatives were ready to fight an election whenever it happens.

"It pretty clear to me we are back in business and that the polls suggest that we are pretty much neck and neck with other parties" he said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Khamenei ties US-Iran peace deal to Israel ending attacks on Lebanon
World.content:
Iran’s supreme leader calls for ‘absolute, unconditional termination’ of Israel’s attacks on Lebanon amid reports of renewed diplomacy.

Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has said that peace between Tehran and Washington is contingent on Israel stopping its attacks on Lebanon.

Khamenei made the statement in a post on X on Sunday.

Iran “has designated the preservation of Lebanon’s territorial integrity, and the absolute, unconditional termination of the Zionist regime’s aggression as the primary condition for any agreement to ending the imposed war against the aggressive US”, he wrote.

Khamenei also voiced his support for the Lebanese group Hezbollah, its former leader, Hassan Nasrallah, and the people of southern Lebanon – the focal point of Israel’s attacks – in a series of posts.

“The Islamic Republic of Iran considers the defense of these oppressed yet powerful mujahideen [of Hezbollah] to be its strategic mandate,” Khamenei said.

Khamenei’s intervention comes amid reports of a halt to attacks and renewed diplomacy between Iran and the United States.

Tehran has insisted that Israel must end its strikes on Lebanon as a condition for Iran ending the war with the US, enshrining that demand in the first clause of the memorandum of understanding it signed with Washington in June.

The agreement has since collapsed amid a dispute over the Strait of Hormuz.

Lebanon was drawn into the conflict in March after Hezbollah launched strikes on northern Israel, citing both the killing of then-Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on the first day of the US-Israel war on Iran, February 28, and Israel’s near-daily bombardment of Lebanese territory, attacks Hezbollah says violated a ceasefire that had ended an earlier round of hostilities in 2024.



On June 26, following the signing of the US-Iran memorandum, Lebanon and Israel signed a US-mediated framework agreement stipulating a phased Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese territory, but without a timetable for the withdrawal.

Instead, it said Israel will withdraw from occupied territories once Hezbollah is disarmed.

Iran and Hezbollah, which was not a party to the talks, have rejected the deal.

While the first phase is Israel’s withdrawal from three “pilot zones”, the Lebanese army said on Sunday that Israeli forces are obstructing the process, including by refusing to withdraw from designated territories.

As of Sunday, Israel was still bulldozing, shelling and conducting combing operations with machineguns across large areas of southern Lebanese territory it is occupying.

At least 4,329 people have been killed, while 37 Israeli soldiers and four Israeli civilians have died in the latest round of violence in Lebanon.

Israel violated a previous ceasefire with Hezbollah more than 10,000 times, according to United Nations peacekeepers.

Mojtaba Khamenei is the son of former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. He was selected as supreme leader after the US and Israel’s assassination of his father.

Mojtaba Khamenei’s statement on Lebanon comes as war spreads into Yemen, with reports of an exchange of attacks between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Trump’s border czar probes possible vetting failures after ICE shooting
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump’s border czar says the vetting of an immigration officer involved in the deadly shooting of a Colombian native in Maine is under internal review after the officer’s relatives revealed to The Associated Press that he had a history of serious mental health struggles and violent behaviour.

Tom Homan said on Sunday that if the allegations against the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer are true, “I don’t think he should ever have cleared vetting.”

“There’s several things under review,” Homan said on CNN about the officer, Army veteran David Brouillette. “The training is under review. I know this specific case, as far as the vetting, is under review by the internal affairs section.”

Questions about the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) rush to hire, train and deploy thousands of new ICE officers to carry out Trump’s immigration crackdown have come into stark focus after back-to-back deadly shootings of immigrants in Maine and Houston.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin ordered a pause in vehicle stops after the Maine shooting, but Trump almost immediately reversed course and insisted the stops resume as a necessary tool in his campaign to round up and deport immigrants without current legal status.

DHS did not immediately respond on Sunday to a request for comment about the internal review.

Homan said that “changes have been made” and that acting ICE director David Venturella has issued a new directive that body cameras must be in use if officers make a vehicle stop.



“Right now, on all vehicle stops, there’s at least one body camera on site to record the entire event,” he said.

He said Venturella “sent an instruction out that he wants at least one body camera on those vehicle stops, so we have everything on video”.

It is unclear if the steps the department is taking will be enough to quell the concerns coming from certain Congress lawmakers over DHS training and tactics as it tries to reach Trump’s mass deportation goals.

Lawmakers push for answers

Lawmakers from both parties have raised concerns.

Democrats pressed ICE officials during a closed-door briefing for the House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee last week, leaving some with more questions than answers.

Lawmakers were told during the briefing that there have been 56 complaints of excessive force against ICE officers – 32 were cleared, and one was referred for disciplinary action.

No discipline had yet been handed out, the lawmakers said they were told. The rest of the incidents are still under investigation.

Meanwhile, Republican Senator Susan Collins of Maine, chair of the powerful Senate Appropriations Committee, has pushed for the use of body cameras and ensured funding for the effort. She had said it was “extremely unfortunate” that the officer involved in the shooting in her home state was not using a camera.

World.title: What’s causing the unprecedented wildfires in Europe?
World.content:
France and Spain have deployed thousands of firefighters, and neighbouring countries have sent help.

Wildfires are ravaging many parts of western and southern Europe, with France and Spain among the hardest hit.

The World Health Organization has warned that climate change is contributing to the frequency and intensity of the fires. This is clear in the record temperatures and successive heatwaves seen across the continent since May. France and Spain have deployed thousands of firefighters, and neighbouring countries have sent assistance. Authorities say the situation is unprecedented.

So, what will it take to extinguish the flames?

Presenter: Per Nyberg

Guests:

Eduardo Rojas – chairman of the board at the Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification

Soraya Fettih – global campaigns coordinator at 350.org, an international environmental organisation focused on addressing the climate crisis

Laurie Laybourn – executive director of Strategic Climate Risks Initiative, a non-partisan think tank

World.title: Israeli government nods to international stabilisation force in Gaza
World.content:
The ISF, to be staffed by ‘friendly countries’, will operate in areas of the Palestinian enclave that are outside Israel’s military control.

Israel’s government has approved the entry of the International Stabilization Force (ISF), part of United States President Donald Trump’s 20-point “peace plan,” to Gaza.

An Israeli official reported on Sunday that Israel’s security cabinet had approved the key legal measures and that the force would operate “in full coordination with” the Israeli military, according to the Times of Israel.
